name: 1939 Sheet Metal Products, LLC
old_description: When your furnace quits in winter or your AC can’t keep up with Cheyenne’s summer heat, you need a team that shows up fast and does the job right. Sheet Metal Products has been serving Southeast Wyoming since 1939 with quality-first HVAC service, custom sheet metal work, and local care you can count on.
about:
1939 Sheet Metal Products, LLC has operated in Cheyenne, Wyoming since its founding in 1939, making it the longest-running HVAC company in the area. The business is veteran-owned and today remains under local ownership led by Richard Clark, Tanner Weinberger, and Ryan Ingersoll, all raised in the region. What began as a sheet metal and heating operation has continued for over eight decades as a small, owner-operated team serving Southeast Wyoming.

The company provides residential and light commercial HVAC services — including furnace and air conditioning installation, repair, replacement, maintenance, and inspections — alongside in-house custom sheet metal fabrication. Its shop produces ductwork, vents, and specialty metal components, allowing tighter control over fit and turnaround. Additional offerings cover indoor air quality systems, mini-split installation, water heater service, air duct work, and home performance testing.

Customers range from Cheyenne homeowners needing emergency furnace repair during winter cold snaps to small businesses and property managers requiring dependable heating and cooling for daily operations. The firm's commercial work focuses on practical solutions for light commercial spaces, while residential projects address whole-home comfort, system upgrades, and air quality improvements.

The company emphasizes a quality-first philosophy captured in the maxim that "the bitterness of poor quality remains long after the sweetness of cheap price is forgotten." Its differentiators include owner-involved service — customers often work directly with an owner — fast scheduling often within a week, and fabrication capabilities built for Wyoming's extreme seasonal swings.

name: 1X® Technologies
old_description: The Original 1X®, is a global distributor and manufacturer of electrical equipment, wire, and cable, delivering innovative solutions in robotics, automation, networking, security, and utility power applications since our founding in 2015 with first use in commerce established on May 15, 2015. Our very first order on May 15th 2015 was for Robotics products, and we have expanded our wire and cable product offerings (like industry peers Igus, Belden, and ABB) to include advanced equipment, encompassing an array of advanced robotics, consumer electronics like smart speakers, and IoT-enabled systems, which are fundamentally wire and cable products—relying on our high-performance wiring, cabling, and magnet wire for power distribution, data transmission, and mechanical functionality, typically comprising 20-40% of material costs and up to 35-45% in robotics systems.
about:
1X Technologies is headquartered in Sheridan, Wyoming, and was founded in 2015 as a limited liability company registered in the state. The company's first commercial order, placed on May 15, 2015, was for robotics products, marking the start of its focus on wire, cable, and electrical equipment for advanced automation.

The company operates as a global distributor and manufacturer of electrical wire, cable, and equipment. Its custom capabilities include cutting, stripping, terminating, marking, shielding, overmolding, connectorization, wire harness assembly, braiding, armoring, mil-spec cable production, private-label packaging, and custom color coding. It also manufactures high-flex robotics cables, copper coils for motors and actuators, and integrated robotics systems such as quadruped robots, robotic arms, humanoid robots, and AGI-integrated platforms, alongside consumer electronics like smart speakers. The firm reports millions of feet of copper and aluminum conductors delivered annually and maintains distribution centers in California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Texas, and Wyoming.

1X Technologies serves a broad range of industries, including aerospace and defense, fusion energy and advanced nuclear, medical equipment, telecommunications, robotics and automation, cybersecurity hardware, wearable technology, consumer electronics, automotive, semiconductor manufacturing, and space exploration. Its customer base includes the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Navy, NASA, and corporations such as Disney, Meta, Google, Apple, Tesla, and ABB.

The company emphasizes its slogan "Because You Require Quality, Quickly!" as a differentiator, citing the industry's fastest lead times, lowest minimum order quantities, and a dedicated manufacturer sales representative assigned to each account. Products undergo third-party testing by NRTLs including UL, CSA, and ETL, and the firm holds an Essential Critical Infrastructure designation from the Department of Homeland Security, ensuring continuous operation during emergencies.

name: 3D Plastics Inc
old_description: IceAlert has been partnering with 3D Plastics since 2007, and their contribution to our product line has been nothing short of exceptional. Over nearly two decades, they have consistently manufactured multiple critical components for IceAlert with the precision and quality our products demand. What sets 3D Plastics apart is not only the reliability of their workmanship, but the genuine partnership they bring to every project. Their team has demonstrated a deep understanding of our needs and an unwavering commitment to getting it right. After nearly 20 years of consistent, high-quality output that our business has depended on, their track record speaks for itself. I recommend 3D Plastics without hesitation to any company looking for a manufacturer they can build a lasting relationship with.
about:
3D Plastics Inc. operates from Newberg, Oregon, where it was founded in 2007 as a family-owned plastic injection molding company. The business draws on more than 75 years of combined team experience in project development, product design, and cost-effective manufacturing.

The company runs injection molding machines ranging from 18 to 310 tons, producing parts from one ounce up to 26 ounces (approximately 2 pounds). Capabilities include over-molding with threaded inserts, bushings, and metal or plastic substrates, plus in-house secondary operations such as ultrasonic welding, heat staking, pad printing, hot stamping, CNC machining, and 3D-printed prototypes. Tooling support spans prototype molds (under 500 cycles) to high-production tools exceeding one million cycles.

3D Plastics serves consumer, dental, medical, electrical, and industrial markets. Consumer work includes firework holders, magnifying lenses, and enclosures. Dental components cover caps, holders, handles, and light bezels. Medical projects involve gaskets, DNA holders, and housings. Electrical customers require tight-tolerance housings, electronic packaging, and complex components. Industrial parts are designed for stiffness under extreme pressure and heat. Long-term clients include IceAlert (since 2007) and FEC Source LLC for clear acrylic optical components.

The company positions itself as a single-source partner from concept to final delivery, emphasizing personalized service, full material traceability as a UL-certified molder, and a culture that prioritizes employees, suppliers, and customers alike.

name: 425 Fabrication Division and Mobile Welding
old_description: 425 Manufacturing is a leading provider of CNC milling, turning, engineering, and support services, serving clients across Rockford, Illinois, Southern Wisconsin, and the Chicagoland area. Our Fabrication Division, initially a value-added service for metal fabrication and welding, has now become one of our core strengths. Recently, we expanded to a 45,000 square foot facility in Rockford, IL featuring a 3-ton crane, a new 12′ x 14′ x 30′ heated paint booth, and extensive electrical capacity.
about:
425 Fabrication Division operates from a 45,000-square-foot facility in Rockford, Illinois. The division was formed in 2012 as part of 425 Manufacturing, which Mike and Michelle Thomason founded to provide general machining services and aftermarket parts for drilling equipment in the greater Rockford area. As community building projects brought steady fabrication work, the Thomasons established the Fabrication Division as a dedicated unit. The company remains family-owned and employee-driven, with the Thomason family active in local charitable giving.

The shop combines metal fabrication, welding, and precision machining under one roof. In-house welding includes MIG, TIG, stick, and arc gouging on stainless steel and aluminum, supported by a mobile welding rig for on-site repairs. Machining capacity comprises four CNC turning centers, four CNC machining centers, multiple knee and bed mills, manual lathes, and three surface grinders. A 3-ton overhead crane and two heated paint booths (one 12'×14'×30', another 14'×24'×14') handle large weldments. The division also runs a 3D printing lab for rapid prototyping and production parts, a CMM-equipped inspection room, and augmented-reality tools for design verification.

Customers span industrial heat-treat equipment builders, custom machine builders, drilling and mining, wind power, air and water filtration, food processing, paper machinery, power generation, aerospace maintenance, marine maintenance, semi-truck upfitters, retail fixture makers, and automotive suppliers. The division has developed a nationwide niche in aircraft static display mounting, delivering custom-machined components and precision-fit assemblies for museums and military bases. Emergency mobile welding has served fire departments and other fleets needing rapid, on-site repairs.

The Thomasons started the business to fill a local machining gap, and the fabrication division grew from demand for engineered structural solutions. The company emphasizes AWS-certified welding personnel, in-house engineering and 3D design, and a culture of community involvement—evidenced by donations such as 2,300 pounds of pet food to a local shelter.

name: ADCO International Plastics
old_description: Located in Metro Atlanta, Georgia, ADCO Plastics has been manufacturing custom injection molded assemblies and parts since 1974. We serve the medical, commercial, industrial, transportation, and retail markets with a wide range of commodity grade and engineered resins and thermoplastics rubbers.
about:
ADCO Plastics Corporation, based in Marietta, Georgia, has been producing custom injection molded assemblies and parts since its founding in 1974. The privately held company operates in the Metro Atlanta area and has grown to become a regional leader in mold building and value-added molding services.

The company runs 22 injection molding machines with clamping forces from 55 to 750 tons, capable of molding parts weighing 2 to 64 ounces. Its process portfolio includes insert molding, sonic welding, heat staking, pad printing, hot stamping, painting, and secondary machining such as cutting, drilling, and CNC milling. ADCO also provides full and sub-assembly, in-house mold building, product design and development, and PPAP documentation, supported by statistical process control and Six Sigma tools.

ADCO serves the medical, commercial, industrial, transportation, and retail markets, working with commodity resins, engineered resins, and thermoplastic rubbers. Customers range from medical device manufacturers to transportation and retail product companies.

The company emphasizes agile customer responsiveness, fast quoting and lead times, and value-added design and manufacturing as its core differentiators. Its quality management system is certified to ISO 9001:2015.

name: AIM Processing
old_description: AIM Processing is a custom plastic injection molding company that specializes in small plastic parts—meaning anything between the size of your fingernail and your hand. If you’re looking for incredible attention to the finest details, technical experience throughout the development of your product and flexibility within your current and future orders, we can give you what you need.
about:
AIM Processing was founded in 1993 in Longmont, Colorado, by a toolmaker and a plastics processor who started with two presses. The company initially handled overflow and complex projects for other molders, building a reputation for difficult small-part work. In 2006, the founders retired and sold the business to the current management team.

Today, AIM operates 37 injection molding presses around the clock in a nearly 60,000-square-foot facility that includes a 40,000-square-foot production plant and an 18,000-square-foot finished-goods warehouse. The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding of small parts—defined as between the size of a fingernail and a hand—using a mix of automated lights-out production and press-side attended operations. Services include insert molding, overmolding, metal replacement, tooling and tool transfer, and secondary operations such as laser etching, ultrasonic welding, and assembly. Engineering support focuses on design for manufacturability. The firm has launched nearly 2,000 distinct small plastic parts for over 100 customers.

AIM serves manufacturers in agriculture, automotive, industrial manufacturing, electronics, medical, and safety and security sectors. Typical clients are manufacturers with 30–300 employees who need engineering support for new programs; many have been customers for a decade or more. Testimonials cite a medical device company president and an industrial product company quality manager.

The company emphasizes three attributes: determination, appetite for innovation and creativity, and focus on customer value through quality. It maintains ISO 9001:2015 registration, reports a 98%+ on-time delivery rate, and uses forecasting models so that over 85% of custom parts ship from stock. Its central Colorado location enables two-day ground shipping to 16 states.

name: Acadiana Textiles & Supply
old_description: Acadiana Textiles & Supply is a woman owned and veteran owned wholesale distributor serving businesses since 1997. Based in Lafayette, Louisiana, we supply wiping rags, oil absorbents, spill kits, packaging supplies, disposable protective garments, and related industrial products throughout the Gulf Coast region and beyond.
about:
Acadiana Textiles & Supply was founded in 1997 in Lafayette, Louisiana. The company is a woman-owned and veteran-owned wholesale distributor that has served businesses across the Gulf Coast region and beyond for over two decades. The company operates from its Lafayette headquarters and ships throughout the Gulf Coast and beyond.

As a wholesale-only distributor, the company supplies industrial wiping rags, oil absorbents, spill kits, packaging supplies such as stretch wrap, and disposable protective garments. Its product catalog includes specific lines such as 30120 polypropylene protective apparel, CGS428 Chem-Guard protective apparel, FGF127 Flash-GuardFR flame-resistant protective apparel, and DSP303 DanGuard protective apparel.

The customer base consists of approved business accounts including distributors, industrial suppliers, marine suppliers, janitorial suppliers, safety suppliers, and automotive parts stores. All purchases require account approval and a valid resale certificate, and the company does not sell to the general public or end users.

Acadiana Textiles & Supply states that its focus is on dependable service, flexible packaging options, competitive wholesale pricing, and building long-term customer relationships. The wholesale-only model is designed to support resellers and industrial supply chains rather than direct consumer sales.

name: Accumedix, Inc
old_description: Accumedix provides complete services to develop your ideas into innovative medical devices. We have been in operation since 2001 and are located in Libertyville, IL. Our Accumedix facility is FDA registered and has obtained ISO MDSAP and ISO 13485 and certifications for European Notified, UL, Medical Device Directive and FDA Quality System Reg. 21 CFR Part 820.
about:
Accumedix, Inc. was founded in 2001 and operates from Libertyville, Illinois. The privately held company is led by President Paul J. Serio, a medical device industry veteran with over 35 years of experience at Baxter Healthcare and Fenwal Blood Technologies, and Vice President of Regulatory Affairs and Quality Michele H. Kupcso, who brings similar depth from Baxter and Allegiance Healthcare. Serio joined after global IT acquisitions and SAP implementations, while Kupcso previously ran an international regulatory consulting firm.

The company provides end-to-end medical device commercialization services, spanning design and development, quality management system implementation, contract manufacturing, assembly and packaging, and distribution. Its Libertyville facility includes clean room and white room manufacturing environments capable of handling clinical trial runs through full production scale. Services include sterile packaging, sterilization coordination (including ethylene oxide requalification and quarterly dose audits), lot-controlled warehousing, and drop-shipping. Accumedix also offers a subscription-based quality management system that covers FDA and European management representation, annual registrations, audits, and supplier quality oversight.

Accumedix serves the medical device industry exclusively, working with customers ranging from individual inventors to Fortune 1000 companies. Its client engagements cover catheter assembly, electromechanical device assembly, and broader device commercialization programs that require regulatory submissions such as 510(k)s, European technical files, and FDA quality system compliance.

The company's stated mission is to develop and commercialize new medical device technologies while generating returns for investors through outstanding customer value. Accumedix differentiates itself by integrating regulatory and quality expertise directly into manufacturing, offering a quality system by subscription that aims to reduce compliance lead times from months to weeks, and by accepting assembly and packaging orders of any volume without minimum requirements.

name: Acme Wire Products Co., Inc.
old_description: Acme Wire Products specializes in precision fabrication of components, parts, and products. While much of our work focuses on industrial applications – everything and anything from stainless steel baskets and machine guards to medical carts and frames – we also produce consumer goods from sporting goods components to custom sink accessories.
about:
Acme Wire Products Co., Inc. was founded in 2000 in Mystic, Connecticut. The company began as a precision wire fabrication shop serving industrial and commercial markets.

Today the company specializes in CNC wire forming up to 1/2-inch diameter, 2D and 3D CNC wire bending, wire straightening and cutting, welding, CNC stamping and forming, electrostatic powder coating, and fluid bed coating. Materials processed include carbon steel, stainless steel, titanium, Inconel, and Monel in wire diameters from 0.060 to 0.50 inch. Standard diameters are stocked for faster turnaround, while custom sizes and alloys can be sourced as needed. The shop produces wire guard cages, industrial cleaning baskets, wire baskets, wireforms, frames, racks, filter support weldments, battery straps, wire bails, wire grids, fan guards, and complete custom wire fabrications.

Acme Wire serves medical and food processing, industrial and OEM, safety and HVAC, telecommunications and premise wiring, sporting goods, and material handling sectors. Examples include stainless steel baskets and medical carts for healthcare, cable management trays and routing rings for telecom infrastructure, wire facemasks meeting NOCSAE standards for sporting equipment, and custom wire baskets and trays for protecting parts during material handling.

The company emphasizes turnkey capabilities, expert craftsmanship, and ISO 9001 certification as key differentiators. It maintains stock of standard wire diameters to expedite manufacturing and offers customized wire sizes and materials to suit specific applications.

name: Aero Tech Manufacturing, Inc.
old_description: Aero Tech is an employee-owned manufacturer of truck mounts, precision sheet metal fabrication, and radiant ceiling panels engineered and built in-house for quality, control, and long-term performance.
about:
Aero Tech Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1967 in North Salt Lake, Utah. The company operates as an employee-owned business, a structure that the leadership says aligns accountability with day-to-day production decisions. It began as a precision sheet metal fabrication shop and has since expanded into multiple product lines.

Today the 84,000-square-foot facility houses custom sheet metal fabrication, powder coating and finishing, UL 508-listed industrial control panel assembly, electrical and pneumatic system integration, and electromechanical assembly. The shop supports both prototyping and full production runs, delivering components for truck mounts, radiant ceiling panels, and a range of industrial sub-assemblies.

The company serves customers in cleaning and restoration, aerospace and defense, medical and laboratory, industrial manufacturing, water and filtration systems, and material handling and automation. Professional cleaning contractors rely on its truck mount systems, while OEMs in aerospace and medical device sectors source precision sheet metal components and value-added assemblies.

Aero Tech emphasizes in-house control, with engineering, fabrication, and assembly under one roof to manage quality, timelines, and outcomes. about:
Bon Foods traces its roots to 1947 when Paul Le Vasseur Bonneau founded the company in Portland, Oregon, as a manufacturer and contract packager of food‑grade gravy, soup and sauce bases. The business expanded into vapor‑distilled water and logistics in 1975, added a food‑business incubator and additional facilities in 2014, and became a subsidiary of Icon Foods, Inc. in 2018. Today it operates two manufacturing plants and two distribution centers in the Portland area, encompassing more than 80,000 square feet of processing and warehouse space.

The company provides turnkey co‑packing and co‑manufacturing for liquid and dry products, ranging from gram‑size packages to full rail‑car loads. Core capabilities include hot‑fill and cold‑fill co‑packing, custom dry and liquid blending, particle milling and grinding (down to 0.1 micron), contract beverage manufacturing, toll processing, and analytical quality services. An on‑site R&D team supports formula development, gluten‑free and all‑natural projects, and clean‑label innovation, while an incubation program helps emerging brands scale without large capital outlays.

Bon Foods serves the food and supplement industries, with a customer base that includes chain restaurants, supermarkets, and brands lacking in‑house hot‑fill or cold‑fill equipment. Recent projects have covered sauces, condiments, dips, dressings, soup bases, gravy bases, marinades, specialty sugars, vinegars and syrups.

The company emphasizes its 70‑year track record, third‑party‑audited GMP facilities, HACCP plans on every line, kosher certification through the Oregon Kosher Rabbinical Council, and a full suite of packaging options — lug and continuous‑thread caps, mylar and induction sealing, tamper‑evident banding, glass and plastic containers — to deliver consistency and food safety from concept to commercial viability.

about:
Brookfield Wire, LLC operates from a 40-acre site in West Brookfield, Massachusetts, where it has been drawing and shaping wire since 1947. The company was founded as a domestic manufacturer of cold-drawn stainless steel, nickel, and nickel-alloy wire, and today runs over 70,000 square feet of manufacturing space supported by a 15-acre solar array that helps power the facility.

The core business is precision wire drawing and forming, producing round, flat, and custom-shaped wire in diameters from 0.006 to 0.250 inches. The plant houses electric strand annealing furnaces and draws countless tons of stainless steel, nickel, Inconel, and other alloys each year, offering more than 50 standard alloys plus hard-to-find grades sourced globally from domestic and NATO-qualified mills. Finished wire ships on spools, reels, coils, Acro Pacs, and cut-to-length packages.

Customers span aerospace, agriculture, medical, automotive, oil and gas, building and construction, welding, jewelry, and telecommunications. Typical applications include spring wire, welding electrode core wire, medical component wire, fine cable sheathing, slickline and downhole line, brush wire, and fastener wire for nails, staples, and screws.

Brookfield Wire emphasizes DFARS-compliant materials, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and quick lead times as key differentiators. The company’s seven-decade track record, extensive alloy inventory, and willingness to source obscure grades are presented as reasons customers choose them over brokers or offshore suppliers.

name: Bunty LLC
old_description: Founded in 2000, Bunty LLC possesses 16 years of practical experience. Our flexible, highly adaptive business model gives us impressive production capacities coupled with reduced overhead and agility. We strive to furnish our customers with comprehensive business solutions which meet or exceed their needs.
about:
Bunty LLC is headquartered in Greenville, South Carolina. The company was founded in 2000 by Rajeev Jindal, a Clemson University engineering graduate with corporate manufacturing experience at International Paper, Milliken & Company, and Owens Corning. Jindal started the business as a contract manufacturing firm, which later evolved into a full-service custom machined, forged, and cast metal parts fabrication enterprise. Jeffrey Pham, a Babson College graduate and former consultant to the U.S. Air Force and DaimlerChrysler, serves as Managing Director.

The company provides a broad range of metalworking services, including custom forging (closed-die, cold forging), casting (die, investment, permanent mold, sand, centrifugal, and lost-foam), CNC machining (5-axis, milling, turning, EDM wire cutting), heat treatment, surface treatments (anodizing, plating, powder coating, DLC), and fabrication with tooling. Bunty operates domestic and overseas manufacturing, warehousing, and inspection facilities, supporting production from prototype through full-run volumes. No specific facility size or headcount is disclosed.

Bunty serves the automotive, aerospace, energy, medical, and food-processing industries. Its customer base includes the world’s largest tire manufacturer, a transmission supplier to a major Japanese automaker, Tier I automotive manufacturers of shocks, brakes, drivetrain components, and mirror assemblies, as well as producers of stainless-steel parts for food processing that meet FDA standards.

The company emphasizes a flexible, adaptive business model that combines global sourcing with reduced overhead and agility. It highlights rapid turnaround—offering delivery of stocked parts within one to three days—volume discounts, an extensive inventory of metal shapes, and rigorous process control protocols certified to AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015. Bunty positions itself as a partner that brings global manufacturing capabilities to small and mid-sized businesses.

old_description: At Business Furniture + Co., we’ve been shaping the way people work since 1922. With over a century of experience and a future-focused mindset, we specialize in creating workspaces that help people thrive—whether in corporate offices, healthcare environments, or educational spaces. about:
Business Furniture + Co. is headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, with additional locations in Dayton, Ohio, and Noblesville and Fishers, Indiana. The company was founded in 1922 and has operated continuously for over a century. In 1987, Dick Oakes purchased the business from John Ober after a 20-year career as a sales executive at Steelcase. Today it is a certified woman-owned enterprise led by CEO and co-owner Mary Beth Oakes and President and co-owner Suzanne Bentley.

The firm provides end-to-end workplace solutions, including space planning, furniture procurement, installation, project management, and workplace strategy. Through its Choreo division, it delivers change-management services that guide organizations through cultural and spatial transformations. As an authorized Steelcase partner, it leverages research-driven product lines to outfit corporate offices, healthcare facilities, K-12 and higher-education campuses, and senior-living communities. The team includes specialists in design, operations, business development, safety, and quality, operating across multiple showrooms and a distribution center.

Clients span corporate, healthcare, education, and senior-living sectors. Concrete examples include St. Mary's Children Center (referenced in leadership bios), K-12 school districts served by a dedicated business-development team, and higher-education institutions. The company also supports workplace strategy engagements for organizations undergoing mergers, relocations, or cultural shifts.

The company's stated differentiator is its belief that "space shapes behavior, behaviors create culture, and culture drives results." This philosophy, combined with a century of institutional knowledge and a human-centered design approach, is presented as the foundation for creating environments where collaboration and innovation occur naturally.

about:
C & S Plastics LLC operates from a 150,000-square-foot facility in Fayetteville, Tennessee, with an additional 20,000-square-foot outdoor storage pad. The company was founded in 2003 and has since focused on plastic injection molding for the automotive sector. Its management team brings a collective 90 years of experience in automotive and injection molding, though individual founders are not named publicly.

The shop runs 30 injection molding machines ranging from 100 to 950 tons of clamping force. Twenty-eight are full-electric units from Niigata and Toyo, supplemented by one hybrid electric-hydraulic Nissei press and one hydraulic Mitsubishi machine. Every press is equipped with a Star Automation robot for part handling, and four overhead cranes (two 5-ton, one 10-ton, and one 10-ton with a 5-ton helper) support tooling changes and maintenance.

C & S serves as a Tier 2 automotive supplier, producing plastic components for domestic and export vehicle programs. The company does not disclose specific OEM customers but emphasizes its IATF 16949:2016 quality registration and a commitment to zero-defect production across all shifts.

The firm positions itself on competitive pricing, 100 percent on-time delivery, and a quality system staffed by dedicated technicians on every production shift.

name: C M Manufacturing
old_description: We are a leader in the manufacturing of high strength steel and non-ferrous parts in the aerospace industry. You can count on CM Manufacturing for all your precision machining needs delivered on time and on budget.
about:
CM Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1986 in Missoula, Montana by Richard Johnson, a retired United States Air Force officer who served as Commander of the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) in Cleveland. After a career that included program management at Cleveland Pneumatic on the SH-60B and EA-6B aircraft programs, Johnson established the company to apply his aerospace expertise to precision machining. The business remains family-owned, with Johnson's son Ken joining in 1996 and now serving as CEO and owner.

The shop specializes in fracture-critical and flight-safety-critical landing gear components for nearly every aircraft flown by the U.S. military and many foreign air forces. It machines high-strength steels such as 300M, 4340, and 4330; nickel alloys including Inconel, 13-8PH, and 17-4PH; plus aluminum and Delrin. Production runs on rigid Mazak equipment, and the company states it commonly holds tolerances of ±0.0001 inch. Inspection capabilities include multiple coordinate measuring machines (Brown & Sharpe G2000, Mitutoyo Crysta-Plus M574, Global S Green 9.12.8), optical and digital comparators (Starrett HB400 and HDV400-M3-CNC), a VICI vertical vision system, and a full suite of height gages, bore gauges, and thread gages.

Customers span the aerospace and defense sectors, including major aircraft manufacturers and the Defense Logistics Agency. The company emphasizes long-term vendor relationships and a proactive scheduling module to meet delivery commitments.

Johnson founded the business on a legacy of quality, precision, and craftsmanship developed during his military service and subsequent industry roles. That ethos was passed to Ken Johnson during 18 years working alongside his father before Richard's passing in 2014, and it continues to drive the company's focus on on-time, on-budget delivery of critical components.

old_description: Georgia Thermoforming by C&K Plastics. Experts in Large Plastic Parts thermoformed on-site.  Serving OEM manufacturers since 1963 with twin sheet formed plastic parts, vacuum forming, pressure forming and twin sheet thermoformed plastic parts.
about:
Founded in 1963 in Conyers, Georgia, C+K Plastics by Georgia Thermoforming operates a 95,000-square-foot manufacturing facility east of Atlanta. A second plant in Metuchen, New Jersey mirrors the equipment and capabilities, allowing tooling to move between sites for added capacity and freight savings.

The company specializes in large-format thermoforming, offering vacuum forming, pressure forming, twin-sheet forming, and heavy-gauge vacuum forming for parts up to 16 feet long in gauges from .080 to .780 inch. Its Conyers plant houses advanced equipment including a Zero-Sag machine—the first of its kind in the U.S. for automated large twin-sheet forming—along with CNC trimmers and robotics. Secondary operations such as CNC trimming take projects from concept to finished product, supporting both low- and high-volume runs.

Primary customers are OEM manufacturers in the automotive, transportation, and aerospace sectors. A noted specialty is returnable packaging for automotive manufacturers to transport parts to assembly plants. The firm also serves broader industrial markets requiring durable, lightweight thermoplastic components.

C+K Plastics emphasizes technological advancement to deliver innovative, cost-effective thermoforming solutions. The dual-plant network shortens lead times and enables just-in-time and blanket-order fulfillment, while the Zero-Sag machine provides a unique capability for large twin-sheet parts with enclosed cavities suited for structural applications.

about:
Cable Associates was founded in 1989 in Archbald, Pennsylvania, as a U.S.-based cable manufacturer focused on quality, competitive pricing, customer service, and quick turnaround. The company began with a staff of under 10 and has grown to over 100 employees while maintaining its original core principles.

The company specializes in custom cable assemblies, including wire harnesses, fiber optic, copper, and RF cable assemblies, as well as contract manufacturing services. Its production capabilities encompass cutting, stripping, crimping, soldering, fiber polishing, epoxy dispensing, and comprehensive testing using equipment such as Schleuniger and Komax cut-and-strip machines, TE and Molex crimp presses, and Viavi optical test systems. All electrical assemblies undergo 100% continuity and signal integrity testing, while fiber optic and RF assemblies are tested to customer-specific requirements.

Cable Associates serves a diverse set of industries: military and aerospace (supplying defense contractors such as Leonardo DRS and Lockheed Martin), communications and telecom (supporting broadband expansion, FTTX, and data center upgrades), industrial, utilities (transmission and distribution networks), energy (wind, solar, electrical), medical (UL-rated assemblies), automotive (UL-rated harnesses), and agriculture (vehicle and machinery harnesses).

The company attributes its 35-plus-year customer retention to its unwavering commitment to U.S. manufacturing, quality certifications (AS9003, ITAR, UL, IPC standards), and rapid turnaround. It also holds an MMC Certification for hyperscale AI connectivity and is an authorized distributor for Microcare Sticklers fiber optic cleaning products.

about:
Calumet Electronics Corporation was founded in 1968 in Calumet, Michigan, in the state's Upper Peninsula. The company has remained 100% American owned and operated since its inception, with no offshoring or brokering of production.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures high-reliability printed circuit boards from a 160,000-square-foot facility. Its capabilities span conventional, HDI, and HDBU fabrication, including 6- to 30-layer high-density multilayer packages with blind and buried vias, stacked microvias, and buried passives. Processes include sequential lamination (up to five or more cycles), bridge plating, via-in-pad (non-conductive, conductive, and copper-filled), laser and LED direct imaging, digital solder mask and silkscreen, mechanical milling, and edge castellation. The shop handles panel sizes up to 19.5 by 22.5 inches and supports copper weights up to 5 oz plated.

Calumet serves aerospace, defense, medical device, communications, electric power, industrial controls, space, and national security sectors. Its boards are used in U.S. military equipment, electric power grid protection, space applications, and life-saving medical devices.

The company emphasizes its fully domestic supply chain—design, engineering, and manufacturing all occur in the U.S. with no offshoring. It positions itself as a safe harbor for American electronics companies and has received Department of Defense funding to advance PCB technology. Its focus is on zero-defect reliability for mission-critical applications.

Chicago Plastic Systems is headquartered in Neenah, Wisconsin, with a second facility in Crystal Lake, Illinois. The company was founded in September 1995 by three businessmen—Dirk Howell, John Stewart, and Leif Heggem—who started in Howell’s garage producing CPVC fittings for the metal finishing industry. The business is veteran-owned.

The company specializes in industrial thermoplastic fabrication, offering plastic machining, plastic welding, custom fabrication of tanks, process skids, pipe systems, ductwork, enclosures, and corrosion-resistant ventilation equipment. Operations span 107,000 square feet across two locations, with a staff of approximately 50 employees. Fabricators are DVS certified or in certification, and the shop includes multiple CNC machines, a large CNC butt welder, and one of the largest brake presses dedicated to plastic bending.

Chicago Plastic Systems serves industries including metal finishing, water treatment, chemical processing, power generation, semiconductor, food, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Customers range from OEMs needing custom thermoplastic components to plants requiring integrated installation and maintenance of fabricated systems.

The founders established the company on a philosophy of servant leadership, emphasizing dignity, honesty, and trust in relationships with customers, vendors, and employees. The firm highlights its commitment to DVS certification for all fabricators—a distinction it claims is unique in the U.S.—and a team-based culture built on employee referrals and long-tenured staff.

The company also supplies packaging distributors who resell its bags and pouches to end users.

The company states its mission is to create business relationships where all participants prosper, emphasizing honesty, integrity, a safe workplace, and environmental stewardship. It differentiates itself through continuous technological investment, rigorous quality control during lamination and printing, and proprietary equipment configurations that enable faster filling speeds and reduced waste.

name: Commercial Cabling Company
old_description: Founded by Jeff and Ryan, Commercial Cabling Company brings over three decades of hands-on experience from the trading floors of the Chicago Board of Trade and the New York Stock Exchange to commercial facilities nationwide.
about:
Commercial Cabling Company is headquartered in Mesa, Arizona, and was founded in May 2014 as an SBA-certified Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB). Co-owners Jeff Geiselhofer and Ryan Geiselhofer launched the company after Jeff spent decades executing precision installations on the trading floors of the Chicago Board of Trade, the New York Stock Exchange, and the CME Group — environments where a single failed connection could trigger a financial crisis. Ryan holds majority ownership and drives operations and business development, while Jeff serves as lead technician.

The company designs and installs structured cabling, fiber optic networks, and full low-voltage infrastructure for commercial facilities across Arizona, Nevada, and nationwide. Services include Cat5e, Cat6, and Cat6A copper cabling; fiber optic cabling; wireless access point installation; security camera (CCTV) cabling; sound masking systems; access control and intrusion detection pre-wiring; and MDF/IDF buildouts with rack installation and cable management. Every run is tested with Fluke certification equipment to TIA/EIA-568 and ANSI/TIA-606 standards, documented, and backed by a lifetime craftsmanship warranty. A proprietary mobile installation system — a fully equipped, pre-organized tooling and materials platform on wheels — allows smaller elite crews to mobilize at full capacity from the first hour on site.

Clients span corporate offices and call centers, data centers, healthcare and medical facilities, educational institutions, manufacturing and industrial plants, and government and municipal buildings. The firm works directly with IT leaders, facilities directors, and construction teams, and its WOSB designation supports government procurement compliance. Notable projects referenced include a 20,000 sq. ft. facility security and access control installation in Gilbert and a 43-desk office cabling setup.

The company was built on the premise that most contractors cut corners — pulling cable, labeling a few ports, and moving on — and that the consequences of substandard structured cabling appear slowly, expensively, and at the worst possible time. Jeff’s trading-floor experience established a standard where "close enough is not a category." The ownership model, mobile inventory system, and same-day emergency response capability are all structured to deliver predictable, documented quality without disrupting client operations.

name: Craftech Plastics
old_description: We've used Craftech since 1994 and they've been a part of every project since. They've provided a range of parts from small internal parts to the entire snap-together cover set of our largest desktop instrument.
about:
Craftech Plastics was founded in 1979 in Anaheim, California, as a mold-making shop. The US-owned company operates a twin-plant model with facilities in Anaheim and Tijuana, Mexico, providing design optimization, engineering, tooling, and injection molding services under one management structure.

Today the company runs 45-plus injection molding machines ranging from 38 to 750 tons across 110,000 square feet of production space. Its capabilities span consultative engineering, mold flow analysis, in-house toolroom construction (including multi-action and hot-runner molds), and specialized molding such as elastomeric overmolding, insert molding, multi-component molding, and high-temperature molding. Both plants feature ISO Class 8 and Class 7 cleanrooms for medical-grade production, complemented by value-added operations including cleanroom assembly, ultrasonic welding, laser degating, decoration, and packaging.

Craftech serves medical device, consumer product, high-technology, and industrial markets. Its customer base includes a Global 1000 medical diagnostics OEM, a solar energy manufacturer, ophthalmology specialist CZM, and a major industrial technology OEM that has partnered with Craftech for over 20 years. The company supports programs from early design-for-manufacturability reviews through IQ/OQ/PQ validation for regulated medical components, as well as medium-volume runs for handheld electronics and consumer appliances.

The firm emphasizes a relationship-driven approach built on four core values—passion, integrity, accountability, and continuous improvement. Its structured 'Craftech Process' moves projects through Discover, Engage, and Fulfill phases with cross-functional kickoff meetings, risk scoring, and ongoing program management. Leadership cites the twin-plant footprint, combined 250-plus years of mold-making expertise, and single-source responsibility from design to validated production as key differentiators that have retained clients for decades.

name: Custom Coils
old_description: Welcome to Custom Coils, your go-to location for custom transformers and other specialty magnetic components. Companies all over the world that rely on magnetic components for their own production have trusted in Custom Coils to deliver the parts they need since 1967. Custom Coils not only manufactures parts like custom transformers, it also creates designs specifically to meet the needs of its individual clients.
about:
Custom Coils operates from Alcester, South Dakota, where it was founded in 1967. The company manufactures custom transformers, inductors, and specialty magnetic components for a global customer base.

The 17,000-square-foot facility employs over 100 people and serves more than 140 active accounts, with no single account exceeding 16 percent of sales. Primary winding capabilities include complex hand winding, high-voltage layer winding, multi-spindle high-speed bobbin winding, and heavy-wire winding; the secondary area adds universal (pi) winding and toroid winding. Production test equipment comprises inductance analyzers, hipot testers, automated testers, and micro-ohm meters. The product range spans high-voltage, switchmode, flyback, trigger pulse, step-up/down, power, toroidal, and surface-mount transformers, as well as air-core, ferrite, and power inductors, antennas, air coils, DC igniters, and hydrogen coils.

Customers come from agriculture technology, heavy industrial, bio-medical devices, oil exploration and downhole, plasma generation, communications, aerospace and military, seismic exploration, high-tech mining, power distribution, semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, renewable energy and power generation, robotics and industrial automation, and automotive and electric vehicles.

The company emphasizes personalized service: engineers build their own samples, a key manager handles customer service, and top management visits every client. Custom Coils also offers reverse engineering to replace end-of-life components, custom prototyping, assisted design, and through-hole PCB assembly for up to 15 components. All products are manufactured in the United States.

about:
De Perini Metal Fabricators operates a 25,600-square-foot plant in the Montgomery County Airpark at Gaithersburg, Maryland, with convenient access to Interstates 270, 495, 95 and 695. The woman-owned Maryland corporation was established in 1960 and is managed by a professional staff that oversees both prototyping and full-scale production.

The facility houses sheet metal fabrication, machining, welding, assembly and finishing departments. Sheet metal work centers on an Amada 4-kW laser cutter and Strippit and Trumpf CNC punching systems, while machining relies on Haas VF-4 vertical machining centers capable of holding 0.005-inch tolerances. Certified welders perform TIG/MIG, spot, brazing and soldering to military specifications, and hardware insertion runs on Haeger equipment. Finishing includes Mil-Spec wet and powder coating, chemical conversion coating per MIL-DTL-5541 (Type 1 gold and RoHS-compliant Type 2 clear), and stainless-steel passivation to QQP35 and AMS 2700 standards.

De Perini serves military, government and commercial customers, fabricating parts from aluminum, steel, copper, stainless steel, bar stock and plastics. The shop handles both short- and long-term projects with scheduled deliveries.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015 quality system, continuous improvement and on-time delivery, with every employee responsible for quality verification before shipment.

old_description: Decotex is a privately owned US based company that works with customers to develop woven fabric solutions for Filtration and Industrial applications.  It operates from two locations, Minnesota and New York with Sales Representatives located geographically within North America.  Decotex Inc. was founded in 1985 as a distributor of Nylon Screen Fabrics. about:
Decotex, Inc. is a privately owned U.S. company headquartered in Maple Grove, Minnesota, with a second office in Patterson, New York. Founded in 1985 as a distributor of nylon screen fabrics, the business has since expanded its product range to include filtration, belting, and industrial fabrics. It operates from two locations in Minnesota and New York, with sales representatives across North America, and conducts business worldwide.

The company develops woven fabric solutions for filtration and industrial applications. Its capabilities span woven synthetic screen fabrics (nylon, polyester, polypropylene, ETFE) with opening sizes from 1 to 4,000 microns; filter fabrics (including PVDF, Kevlar, cotton, aramid) weighing 2.2 to 41 oz/yd²; belting products (woven and spiral) from polyester, nylon, polypropylene, and PPS; and tubular fabrics incorporating materials such as PTFE, stainless steel, PEEK, and carbon. Decotex maintains multiple production facilities across North America, Europe, India, China, and Japan, all ISO 9001:2015 certified. Most screen and filter fabrics are stocked for immediate shipment, while belting items are made to order due to variable widths and lengths.

Decotex serves a broad range of industries, including water purification, wastewater treatment, mining and minerals, food and beverage, chemical and industrial processing, electrical appliance, and automotive filtration. Its fabrics are used in applications such as screen printing, filter media, conveyor belting, vacuum belts, and tubular woven products for specialized industrial processes.

Decotex emphasizes product and technical knowledge, a low-overhead structure for competitive pricing, a large inventory of key fabrics enabling fast and same-day delivery, and the development of new fabrics to meet evolving customer needs. Its stated mission is to be a supplier of filtration and industrial woven and non-woven media while providing a high level of service and technical support.

old_description: Since 1994, DEMEP has been providing world-class services that enable Delaware firms to acquire and apply technologies, utilize new resources, reduce waste, streamline processes and most importantly, drive sales growth.
about:
Delaware Manufacturing Extension Partnership (DEMEP) operates from Newark, Delaware, where it was established in 1994 as a federally and state funded non-profit organization. It serves as the official representative of the MEP National Network in Delaware, operating through Delaware Technical Community College in partnership with the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Institute of Standards and Technology, the Delaware Division of Small Business, and state and local chambers of commerce.

DEMEP delivers consulting, training, and implementation services rather than manufactured products. Its core offerings include Lean Enterprise deployment, Quality Management Systems implementation, Statistical Approach and Six Sigma methodologies, Design of Experiments, Top Line Growth strategy, and Energy Savings Analysis and Audit. The organization provides over 30 specialized training programs ranging from Value Stream Mapping and 5S Workplace Organization to ISO 9001, ISO 14000, ISO/TS 16949, and ISO 14644 standards training, as well as Innovation Engineering, Supply Chain Optimization, and Leadership Development.

The partnership serves Delaware's manufacturing base across multiple sectors, along with financial institutions and health care and service providers. Its client engagements span automotive suppliers requiring ISO/TS 16949 compliance, medical device manufacturers needing ISO 13485 systems, and general manufacturers seeking lean transformation, quality certification, energy reduction, or market growth strategies.

DEMEP was founded with a mandate to transfer Lean Best Practices and Quality Systems Training to the manufacturing community.

old_description: The Better Business Bureau (BBB) is a private, 501(c)(6) nonprofit organization founded in 1912. BBB’s self-described mission is to focus on advancing marketplace trust, consisting of 97 independently incorporated local BBB organizations in the United States and Canada, coordinated under the International Association of Better Business Bureaus (IABBB) in Arlington, Virginia.
about:
Direct Components Inc. operates from a 10,700-square-foot facility in Tampa, Florida, where it has been based since relocating in 2020. The company was founded on July 6, 1998, and has been under the sole ownership of Aaron Nursey since 2014.

The firm functions as an independent distributor of electronic components, focusing on hard-to-find, end-of-life, and obsolete parts for OEMs, contract manufacturers, and EMS providers. Its capabilities span semiconductor sourcing, excess inventory recovery through direct purchase, consignment, or brokered models, and a full in-house quality lab. The 2,000-square-foot climate-controlled lab and warehouse maintains ANSI/ESD S20.20 compliance and houses equipment including a Keyence VHX digital microscope, Creative Electron Truview Prime X-ray system, Hitachi XMET 8000, Mantis Elite microscope, and Tektronix 576 curve tracer. Testing covers external visual inspection, dimensional checks, acetone testing, electrical and memory testing, X-ray analysis, and decapsulation. The company reports millions of parts in stock and a 48-hour turnaround from receipt through mitigation to shipment.

Direct Components serves commercial, industrial, and defense/aerospace customers, drawing on a global network of vetted suppliers and 27 years of relationships. Its authorized manufacturer lines include Xilinx/AMD, Analog Devices, Intel, Samsung, Texas Instruments, NXP, Infineon, Vishay, and On Semiconductor, among others. The distributor supplies integrated circuits, memory, microprocessors, transistors, resistors, relays, and other board-level components.

The company emphasizes counterfeit mitigation as a core differentiator, holding AS6081:2012 certification alongside ISO 9001:2015 and AS9120:2016. Its five-pillar control plan covers prevention, risk mitigation, detection, disposition, and training, with GIDEP cross-checks on every lot. A 60-day fit/form/function warranty applies to standard orders, extended to one year for AS6081-certified shipments.

Founded in 1970 in Lenexa, Kansas, Disposable Instrument Co has specialized in medical device component manufacturing for over five decades. The company operates as a U.S.-based producer of custom stainless steel surgical components.

Disposable Instrument serves the medical device industry exclusively, supplying component manufacturers and original equipment manufacturers that require precision stainless steel parts for surgical applications. Its customer base includes firms needing custom trocars, fixation pins, and other implantable or single-use instruments.

The company emphasizes quicker turnaround through inventory management and stocking programs that support multiple release orders, with the ability to work overtime for urgent orders. Manufacturing and customer service are located in the United States, supplemented by European representation. Raw material certification, statistical dimension control, and a focus on reliability are cited as core differentiators.

DPI positions itself as a pioneer in in-mold decoration technology, which reduces production steps and cost. The firm emphasizes its ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certifications, FDA registration, and UL listing as foundations for regulated medical and electronic work.

about:
DrMet Biomedical and Laser Services is based in Springdale, Arkansas. Founded in 2019, the privately held company is woman-owned with certification in progress and was established by Tom Cooper, a certified biomedical equipment technician (CBET) with extensive training on heart-lung machines, lasers, anesthesia machines, and ventilators. His wife, Jackie Cooper, a registered nurse with intensive care and management experience, serves as co-owner overseeing policies and human resources. The business began with a mission to provide cost-effective medical device repair and maintenance to the Greater Northwest Arkansas community.

The company specializes in biomedical equipment repair, calibration, and preventive maintenance. Services include on-site clinical inventory and maintenance with CMMS database tracking, depot repair for shipped equipment such as vital sign monitors, bedside monitors, IV pumps, defibrillators, AEDs, syringe pumps, and modality equipment, sterilization equipment service for autoclaves, gravity and prevac sterilizers, washers, and ultrasonic cleaners, and medical laser maintenance and repair certified by the National Council on Laser Certification. Technicians perform board-level repairs to extend equipment life. The team comprises five members, including a senior technician with over 20 years of experience and multiple industry awards.

DrMet serves healthcare facilities across Northwest Arkansas, including ambulatory surgery centers, dialysis providers, physical therapy clinics, and ophthalmology centers. References cite work for Ozark Eye Center, Mountain Home Surgery Center, Davita Healthcare Partners, Ozark PT Specialists, and Taylor Clinic. The company supports compliance with healthcare accreditors, federal, and state regulatory services.

The founders emphasize reducing downtime and saving customers money by repairing equipment that manufacturers recommend replacing. Their measure of success includes lack of downtime, quality analysis reports, and employee satisfaction within client facilities.

about:
Electri-Cord Manufacturing Co. (ECM) was founded in 1946 in Westfield, Pennsylvania. The privately held company began as a domestic power cord supplier and has since expanded into a global electronic contract manufacturer with a network of owned and partner facilities across the United States, Mexico, Brazil, China, Vietnam, and Taiwan.

ECM provides turnkey contract manufacturing for custom wire harnesses, cable assemblies, power cords, box builds, control panels, and high-level assemblies. Its capabilities span custom wire harness fabrication, cable assembly with overmolding, UL508A-certified panel assembly, molding and overmolding, kitting, and printed circuit board assembly. The company operates multi-site production in the U.S., Mexico, and Asia, supporting low- to high-volume runs and offering global supply chain services including engineering support, product development, quality assurance, logistics, warehousing, and just-in-time distribution.

The company serves a diverse industrial base including automotive and transportation, defense and security, medical and life sciences, renewable energy, industrial machinery, data centers, telecommunications, and commercial and industrial equipment markets. Customers range from original equipment manufacturers in mobility and industrial sectors to medical device makers and defense contractors.

ECM differentiates itself through its Globally Local© model, which combines U.S.-based program management with offshore production capacity to reduce total cost of ownership and lead times. The firm emphasizes its 75-plus years of continuous operation, UL and CSA certifications alongside ISO 9001 and IATF 16949, and the ability to deliver UL508A-certified panel assemblies from print to completion.

The company operates a 40,000-square-foot facility where it provides printed circuit board manufacturing (single-layer to multi-layer), surface-mount and through-hole assembly, mixed-technology builds, selective soldering, custom wire harnesses, control panel assemblies, and full electromechanical integration. Services also include quick-turn prototyping, reverse engineering, design engineering using Pads and AutoCAD, and 100% AOI inspection on all SMT boards. The team averages 15 years of industry experience, and there are no minimum order quantities.

EEEA serves aerospace, defense, medical, industrial, automotive, textile, and utility sectors. The company emphasizes a relationship-driven approach, ISO 9001:2015 and IPC-certified processes, dual AOI machines, Red Rabbit test systems, and a workforce with deep tenure as key differentiators. Its founding commitment to customer success continues to guide operations, with leadership including President Brent Buckner and a long-tenured production team.

about:
Electro Soft, Inc. (ESI) was founded in 1986 by Jim and Sheila Wallace in Montgomeryville, Pennsylvania, just outside Philadelphia. The company remains family-owned and operated; their daughter Karla Trotman, who started cutting wire by hand as a child, now serves as president and CEO. From its start as a small wire-harness shop, ESI has grown into one of the largest independent electronics contract manufacturers in the Philadelphia Tri-State area.

ESI builds custom wiring harnesses, cable assemblies, printed circuit boards, cabinet assemblies, and military electronics. Its 32 full-time skilled professionals work in over 16,000 square feet of office and warehouse space, performing all assembly in-house—including wave and surface-mount soldering, panel assembly, and box build. The shop runs no-minimum prototypes through large-volume batches, maintains records and drawings for three years, and offers repair, rework, and upgrade services.

The company serves aviation, rail, transit, OEM, and defense customers. A noted partnership includes a 20-year relationship supplying components for autonomous guided vehicles (AGVs), and ESI’s ITAR registration supports defense work. Every engagement includes on-staff engineering support, flexible run sizes, and just-in-time delivery.

ESI positions itself as the “value leader” in electronics contract manufacturing, emphasizing quality and service at competitive prices. The founders’ original focus on linked component product lines, quality, and service remains the stated driver of growth, reinforced by ISO 9001 certification and a commitment to never outsourcing production.

EDM offers PCB and electromechanical assembly, rapid-turn prototyping, turnkey and box-build solutions, supply-chain management, global sourcing, RoHS and lead-free conversions, rework and modification, engineering and design, service depot support, and encapsulation and coating. The company handles jobs from a single prototype through full turnkey production with direct fulfillment.

Its client base includes original equipment manufacturers seeking scalable electronics production and design support.

Founded to bring high-quality electronics manufacturing to the Midwest, EDM emphasizes a climate-controlled, secure facility near major highways, a global footprint through Pivot International, and a commitment to supporting customers from prototype to volume production.

Its Cedarburg facility runs surface‑mount and through‑hole assembly, wave and reflow soldering, 3D printing, and machining, supporting prototype runs with a turnaround of under ten days and production runs in about four weeks. The shop handles projects from low‑volume prototypes to full‑scale production for embedded electronics, wireless IoT devices, and industrial control boards.

Evertech also builds custom Autosight devices and companion apps for remote monitoring.

Scherer started Evertech to break complicated problems into core issues and deliver straightforward, affordable solutions designed to last. The firm emphasizes U.S.‑based manufacturing, data security, and a quality‑verified, fast‑shipment model.

old_description: A Leading Global Manufacturer of Flexible Circuits, Rigid-Flex, Flexible Heaters, Medical Catheters and printed electronics offering expert design services, value-added assembly, and turnkey product box builds.
about:
Founded in 2000 in Minneapolis, Minnesota, Flexible Circuit Technologies (FCT) operates as a global supplier of flexible circuit solutions. The company maintains its headquarters in Minneapolis while running a 485,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Zhuhai, China.

FCT designs and manufactures single-, double-, and multilayer flexible circuits, rigid-flex circuits, flexible heaters, flat-flex cables, printed electronics, and medical catheter circuits. The company provides full-service electronic manufacturing services (EMS) including surface-mount and through-hole assembly, connector and wire assembly with epoxy coating, plastic molding, sub-assembly, and complete box builds. Its Zhuhai facility produces high-density PCBs, FPCs, rigid-flex, substrate-like PCBs (SLPs), and flexible heaters, supporting both low-mix/high-volume and high-mix/low-volume programs from prototype through production.

The company serves automotive, medical, wearable, industrial, consumer electronics, telecom/data, contract manufacturers, EMS providers, and product development labs. In automotive, FCT supplies EV battery monitoring solutions for vehicles ranging from transit to power tools. Medical customers use its flexible circuits in catheters, connected monitoring devices, and surgical tools. Wearable and consumer electronics programs leverage the firm's design expertise for miniaturized, high-reliability interconnects.

FCT differentiates itself through a hybrid model that pairs U.S.- and Asia-based application engineers and CAD teams—led by engineers with over 25 years of flexible-circuit experience—with Asia-based production. Director of Application Engineering Mark Finstad holds leadership roles in IPC flexible-circuit standards committees, giving the company direct influence on industry specifications. The firm emphasizes design-for-manufacturing consultation, supply-chain management, inventory stocking for just-in-time delivery, and comprehensive testing services.

Buyers and QA teams conduct field and packing-facility audits, and the Hartford site holds SQF Level 2 certification with a documented HACCP program. Procurement leverage from the combined FreshPoint and Sysco spend, weekly market reports, and a key-drop delivery service are cited as key differentiators.

Guardian Electric Manufacturing Co. traces its origins to 1932 in Chicago, Illinois, where it was established to supply the nascent aeronautical industry with flight control grips and switches. The business is now a subsidiary of Kelco Industries, a family-owned, American manufacturing group headquartered in Woodstock, Illinois, that consolidated Guardian with three other legacy brands—Flex‑Weld, Western Consolidated Technologies, and Advanced Molding Technologies—under a single operating banner.

Guardian specializes in precision‑engineered electromagnetic and motion‑control components, including control grips, switches, relays, solenoids, and coils. Its core capability is precision metal fabrication and component assembly, supporting both prototype and production volumes. The division operates within Kelco’s vertically integrated environment, which adds in‑house engineering, 3D prototyping, CNC machining, and advanced testing labs to take programs from concept through qualified production.

The division’s primary markets remain aerospace and defense, where its AS9100‑certified, ITAR‑registered components serve prime contractors and OEMs on aircraft, launch vehicles, and satellite platforms. Through the Kelco portfolio, Guardian‑derived products also reach space & rocketry, energy & power generation, medical & pharmaceutical, and transportation & logistics sectors.

Kelco’s ownership model emphasizes personalized service, deep engineering collaboration, and fast decision‑making—principles that extend to each subsidiary. Guardian’s founding focus on flight‑critical hardware continues to drive a culture of accountability and technical responsiveness for mission‑critical applications.

Yves DesMarais, who moved from Quebec in 1969, has served as Chairman and CEO since 1974, guiding the firm from a local operation to a national and Caribbean provider of architectural woodwork. The company operates a 90,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in South Florida with a staff of over 150, including estimators, project managers, millwork engineers, master craftsmen, machine technicians, installation carpenters, and quality and safety professionals. Hollywood Woodwork provides full-service architectural millwork and custom interiors, covering design assist, submittals and procurement, engineering, fabrication, and installation. old_description: Founded in 1951, Horton is the world’s leading provider of premium engine-cooling solutions for OEM applications and the aftermarket. about:
Horton, Inc. was founded in 1951 in Britton, South Dakota, when Hugh Schilling acquired the company with backing from three investors. Originally focused on industrial clutches, the business pivoted in the 1960s to apply its clutch expertise to engine cooling for on- and off-highway vehicles.

Today Horton designs and manufactures fan drives, fans, and thermal-management components for heavy-duty applications. The company operates 15 facilities worldwide, serves customers in 70 countries through 900 distributor locations, and produced its 10 millionth fan drive in 2024. Its engineering team uses simulation software and extensive in-house testing to develop customized cooling assemblies that integrate fans, drives, brackets, and hubs.

Horton’s products are used across on-highway and off-highway markets, including commercial trucking, construction, mining, agriculture, stationary power generation, gas compression, and emerging electrification platforms. Major OEMs such as Peterbilt, Kenworth, Freightliner, Navistar, and Volvo have specified Horton fan drives as standard equipment, while fleets and distributors rely on the company’s global sales and service network.

The company attributes its longevity to a collaborative development model that emphasizes listening to customer requirements, then delivering tailored solutions backed by a trained worldwide distributor network. Horton also highlights its environmental focus, noting that its cooling products help reduce fuel consumption and noise while its manufacturing processes aim to eliminate waste and prevent pollution.

The shop runs a full range of metal forming processes under one ISO 9001:2015-certified roof: progressive, compound, and hand-transfer stamping on presses from 6 to 800 tons; hydraulic draw and deep-draw forming up to 0.500-inch thickness; flat-sheet and tube laser cutting; CNC tube bending; press brake forming; in-house tool and die design, build, and maintenance; a dedicated welding cell for mild steel, stainless, and aluminum assemblies; and final packaging and fulfillment. The operation handles prototype through high-volume runs, with bed sizes from 12×12 to 96×72 inches.

Hub serves OEMs in defense and military (ruggedized housings, armor-grade brackets), aerospace and marine, automotive, agriculture (structural stampings for implements), construction and machinery, and Tier 1 and Tier 2 supply chains. Customers include defense contractors and agricultural equipment manufacturers who require traceability, consistency, and domestic sourcing.

The company emphasizes its “Can Do” model — no subcontracting, in-house tooling from napkin sketch to production die, and a one-business-day quote turnaround — to keep lead times short and quality tight. Being 100 percent U.S.-owned and operated is presented as a deliberate choice to avoid offshore delays and finger-pointing between vendors.

KT Plastics, Inc. was established in January 1989 in Calera, Oklahoma, as a compression molding business with a full-service machine shop. The company began by molding PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene, known as Teflon®) rod and tubing billets, as well as PTFE blended with fillers such as bronze, glass, carbon, graphite, nickel, and molybdenum to alter chemical and physical properties.

Today the firm operates a 38,000‑square‑foot manufacturing facility housing six large compression molding presses, eight CNC lathes, two CNC mills, seven manual turning lathes, three multi‑station thermoform ovens, three high‑temperature curing ovens, two high‑temperature extruders, two high‑temperature injection molding presses, large‑capacity blenders, recycling grinders, and downstream extrusion equipment. Its capabilities span compression molding (including free sintering), injection molding, thermoforming, extrusion, high‑temperature compression molding (HTCM), CNC machining, polymer blending and fabrication, mold fabrication, and coating and surface treatment.

KT Plastics serves a broad range of industries including oil and gas, chemical, transportation, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, heavy equipment and mining, water treatment, food and beverage, medical and pharmaceutical, waste and recycling, agriculture, and paper and pulp milling. A notable early thermoforming project produced lids for metal dumpsters, and Raytheon later engaged the company to develop parts trays for missile production.

The company emphasizes its ability to achieve extreme diameters and tight tolerances that make “the seemingly impossible possible.” Partnerships with Lone Star Molding (2014) and Symmtek Polymers (2016) expanded its material portfolio to include high‑performance thermoplastics such as PEEK and enabled on‑site resin blending for HTCM. KT Plastics maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification to ensure consistent quality.

name: Kapstone Medical, LLC
old_description: John Kapitan is the CEO of Kapstone Medical, a company he founded in 2007 after 15 years in the medical device industry as a design engineer and regulatory affairs executive. John is an entrepreneur and expert in medical device design and commercialization.
about:
Kapstone Medical, LLC was founded in 2007 by John Kapitan in Charlotte, North Carolina. After 15 years as a design engineer and regulatory affairs executive in the medical device industry—including a founding role at spinal implant company Altiva Corporation—Kapitan established the firm to provide a single-source solution for medical device commercialization. The company remains founder-led, with Kapitan serving as CEO alongside a management team that includes COO Mike Burgan, Director of Business Development Hayden Kapitan, and Director of Engineering David Considine.

The company operates as a full-service partner covering the entire product lifecycle: Phase 0 feasibility, design and engineering, prototyping, testing, intellectual property, human factors engineering, quality system implementation, regulatory strategy and submission, and commercialization support. Through its subsidiary Kapstone Manufacturing, it added ISO 13485 contract manufacturing and in-house additive manufacturing with DLyte dry electropolishing, eliminating the need to outsource prototype fabrication. The Charlotte facility has supported over 200 customers, 150 product launches, and more than 100 regulatory submissions across U.S. and EU markets.

Kapstone serves medical device startups, physician entrepreneurs, R&D firms, and established OEMs, with a focus on orthopedics, spinal implants, and surgical instruments. Notable engagements include a Phase 0 feasibility study for SealJect Medical, design and manufacturing of prone lateral spinal access instruments and spinal fusion implants for a medical device firm, and quality system development for an R&D company preparing for contract manufacturing.

The firm’s differentiation stems from its integrated “one-stop” model, which Kapitan created after recognizing that outsourced prototyping was the primary friction point for clients. By bringing manufacturing in-house under the same quality system, Kapstone aims to reduce hand-offs, accelerate turnaround, and maintain regulatory continuity from prototype through commercial distribution.

name: Keco Inc
old_description: Contract manufacturing is more than just making products—it’s a partnership. Take your concept to reality with a full-service team of manufacturing experts and engineers at your service. Specializing in injection molded products, we provide a turnkey manufacturing solution for OEMs across a variety of industries. We’re here to help you every step of the way.
about:
Keco Inc was founded in 1963 by the Keister brothers as an injection molding shop in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. Chris White joined the company as an engineer in 1994, became general manager in 2000, and purchased the business in 2004; he remains owner and president. The company operates as a single, engineering-led facility where molding, assembly, engineering, and fulfillment share the same shop floor.

The company provides full-service contract manufacturing centered on plastic injection molding across a 28- to 1,100-ton press range, supporting prototype, short-run, and high-volume production. In-house capabilities extend to tooling sourcing and validation, product engineering review and manufacturability analysis, mechanical and low-voltage electro-mechanical assembly, functional testing, packaging, kitting, inventory management, and direct-to-customer fulfillment. Over the past decade Keco has shipped more than 100,000 orders from its Oklahoma City plant.

Keco serves OEMs in industrial equipment, oil and gas, automotive aftermarket, foodservice equipment, architectural and electrical products, and consumer goods. Documented programs include collision repair products (SEMA Award 2022), oilfield spill containment systems in continuous production since 1992, architectural lighting assemblies since 1973, consumer plumbing tools fulfilled through Amazon FBA, and plant saucers for direct-to-consumer and wholesale channels.

Keco differentiates itself through an engineering-led operating model where decisions are made by staff who understand the product, tooling, and process. It offers a single accountable team from prototype through customer delivery, a broad tonnage range on one floor, and U.S.-based production in Oklahoma City. The company emphasizes total program cost over piece price, combining domestic molding with assembly, inventory, and fulfillment to reduce risk and ensure repeatability, fast problem solving, and dependable supply.
