old_description: Founded in 1984 and staffed by over 150 skilled associates, the ISO 9001:2015-certified Nashville metal fabrication operation is focused solely on fabrication rather than raw material distribution and ensures top-tier quality through advanced inspection tools, in-house welder training, and a customer-first approach, all backed by the global strength and reliability of Kloeckner Metals.
about:
Kloeckner Metals Nashville operates a 115,000-square-foot sheet metal fabrication facility in Lebanon, Tennessee, about 30 minutes east of Nashville. The operation began in 1984 as American Fabricators, Inc., and today functions as the only Kloeckner Metals site dedicated exclusively to value-added fabrication rather than raw material distribution. It is owned by Kloeckner Metals Corporation, a subsidiary of the German-based Klöckner & Co SE Group.

The plant employs over 150 associates and houses 17 Amada turret punches, four Amada lasers (including 6 kW and 4 kW fiber and two 4 kW CO₂ units), 24 Amada press brakes up to 220 metric tons, a 60-ton robotic press brake, a Panasonic TM-2000WG III robotic welding arm, and a Prima Power BCe Smart Panel Bender. Capabilities span laser cutting, forming, MIG/TIG/resistance spot welding, hardware insertion, mechanical assembly, and metal finishing such as media blasting, tumbling, grinding, graining, and polishing. Materials processed include hot-rolled pickled and oiled, cold rolled, galvanized, galvannealed, aluminized, prepainted, electro-galvanized, aluminum, and stainless steels.

The facility serves the food-service, transportation, HVAC, hot-water-heater, and appliance industries. Examples from the branch include stainless-steel fan mounts for food service, galvanized mounting brackets and door-frame headers for transportation, stainless drain pans and pre-painted galvanized posts for HVAC, hot-rolled plate disc plates for water heaters, and cosmetic stainless parts for appliances.

The company emphasizes its in-house welder qualification program based on AWS D1.1, advanced inspection tools, and a workforce where over half the associates have tenured more than ten years. Special programs include Kanban, stocking, quick-turn prototypes, and PPAP support, all backed by the global supply-chain strength of Kloeckner Metals.

The company emphasizes vertical integration, offering in-house machining, metal-backed PCB production, and rapid lead times of 24 hours to 15 days. Its focus on advanced PTFE hybrid packaging for manifolds, radiators, antennas, radomes, and tiles, combined with heavy copper capability above 5 oz, positions it for high-power RF and thermal-management applications.

about:
M Plastics Inc. is a family-owned manufacturer based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2005. The company began as a custom poly bag and film operation, keeping every production step under one roof.

The company provides full-service custom poly bag and film manufacturing, including in-house LDPE extrusion, flexographic printing up to six colors, and bag making. Its Los Angeles facility produces flat bags, gusseted bags, wicket bags, bread bags, ice bags, rock bags, anti-static bags, suffocation warning bags, baler bags, as well as LDPE film, poly tubing, shrink film, stretch wrap, custom sheeting, box liners, drum liners, pallet covers, furniture bags, VCI corrosion protection liners, and trash liners. All products are made to order with nationwide shipping from the same site.

M Plastics serves a broad range of industries, including meat and protein, poultry, seafood, bakery, produce and grocery, frozen foods, food processing, manufacturing, pharmaceutical, agriculture, construction, e-commerce, retail and apparel, electronics and ESD, and landscaping. The company emphasizes food-grade material options for food processors and manufacturers across the country.

Its family-owned structure and commitment to quality and customer satisfaction drive its approach to tailored packaging solutions.

name: M.A.R.'s Engineering Company
old_description: M.A.R.'s Engineering is a precision machining company offering screw machining and CNC services. Since 1964 has produced high-accuracy turned components for aerospace, medical and electronic industries.
about:
M.A.R.'s Engineering Company has operated from San Leandro, California since 1964. The family-owned business began as a precision screw machining shop and has remained under family stewardship for nearly six decades.

The company specializes in high-accuracy turned components, running 35 Brown & Sharpe single-spindle screw machines capable of up to five simultaneous operations. Its capabilities extend to multi-spindle screw machining, centerless grinding, CNC milling and water jetting, CNC turning, wire EDM, and in-house finishing — including plating (hard chrome, zinc, black oxide, nickel, gold, Teflon), polishing, and light assembly. A workforce of 50–99 employees handles prototype through production volumes in a single facility.

M.A.R.'s serves aerospace, medical, electronics, automotive, chip manufacturing, food processing, heating and cooling, transportation, electrical/utilities, and music industries. Customers range from OEMs requiring complex prototypes to those needing large production runs of precision parts.

The company emphasizes a quality system built on dual order review, first-article inspection of five to eight pieces per setup, and a three-stage in-process monitoring method where operators batch parts for dimensional verification. Inspectors walk the line twice daily to confirm conformance. This structure, combined with family ownership, is cited as the basis for responsive service and competitive pricing.

name: MANAR | Tennplasco | Plastic Injection Molder & Contract Manufacturer
old_description: We are deeply committed to manufacturing in the USA, supporting American jobs and contributing to the domestic economy. As a 100% employee-owned company since 2016, we build on the rich legacy of founder Gene Nolen, a pioneer in plastic injection molding, empowering our team to invest in customer success.
about:
Manar, Inc. (also operating as Tennplasco) is headquartered in Lafayette, Tennessee. Founded in 1974 by Gene Nolen, a pioneer in plastic injection molding, the company has operated for over 45 years. In 2016, it transitioned to 100% employee ownership, empowering its workforce of approximately 330 employee-owners to invest directly in customer success.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding, offering thermoplastic injection molding, gas-assist molding, and scientific molding across horizontal and vertical presses ranging from 55 to 2,300 tons. It operates multiple facilities: one plant certified to ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 with a white room for medical molding, a second plant certified to ISO 13485 and IATF 16949, and two additional plants certified to IATF 16949. Capabilities extend to in-house tool design, seamless tool transfers, prototyping via additive manufacturing/3D printing, automated assembly, and value-added services such as painting, kitting, and packaging. Process validation (IQ, OQ, PQ) supports early-stage projects.

Manar serves a diverse industrial base including medical device, lawn and garden, consumer products, powersports, automotive and transportation, industrial, aerospace, and power and energy sectors. Its customer roster includes long-standing OEMs; the company notes its very first customer remains a client today.

Founded on Gene Nolen's vision to advance plastic injection molding, Manar emphasizes domestic manufacturing, maintaining all production in the USA. The employee-ownership model, adopted in 2016, aligns the team's incentives with customer outcomes, fostering a culture of accountability and long-term partnership.

about:
MBS Fabrication, Inc. operates from Southbridge, Massachusetts, where it was founded in 1997 as a woman-owned business. The company began with a focus on precision sheet metal work and has grown into a specialist in close-tolerance fabrication, forming, and machining.

The shop combines CNC machining, welding, and sheet metal fabrication to produce precision components and sub-assemblies such as cap and baffle assemblies, tube and housing sub-assemblies, dynamic plate sub-assemblies, and effusion plate sub-assemblies. Its quality assurance personnel inspect every part to verify conformance to customer requirements, drawing on a team whose combined experience exceeds 100 years.

While the company serves customers large and small, its certifications — ISO 9001:2015, AS9100:2016, and NADCAP for nonconventional machining and welding — indicate a strong orientation toward aerospace and defense supply chains. The product portfolio reflects the complex, high-reliability assemblies typical of those sectors.

MBS states its mission is to create products held to the highest standards, meet or exceed customer expectations, continuously improve, and deliver jobs on time, every time. This commitment to craftsmanship and timeliness has been the foundation of its reputation for over 25 years.

about:
MECA Electronics, Inc. was founded in 1961 in Denville, New Jersey. The privately held corporation operates under the name Microwave Equipment & Components of America and has manufactured RF and microwave components in the United States for over six decades.

The company designs and produces a broad line of passive RF and microwave components, including fixed attenuators, directional couplers, hybrid couplers, isolators, circulators, power dividers and combiners, RF loads, DC blocks, bias tees, cables, and adapters. Its portfolio extends to integrated assemblies and a high-reliability ML series qualified to military specifications such as MIL-DTL-23971, MIL-DTL-15370, MIL-DTL-39030E, and MIL-STD-202. Products cover frequencies up to 50 GHz and are built by J-STD certified assemblers with standard and enhanced screening options.

MECA serves public safety, rail and transportation, commercial wireless (including distributed antenna systems), 5G/6G and VSAT/SATCOM millimeter-wave markets, as well as aerospace, defense, and space programs. Rail products meet EN50155 environmental standards, while low-PIM components address commercial wireless infrastructure with no power derating to 85 °C. The company also provides value-added kitting and integration of customer-supplied parts.

MECA emphasizes rugged, U.S.-made construction backed by a 36-month warranty. Its differentiators include IP67/68-rated enclosures, thermal and electrical screening processes, and a focus on traceability for ground, air, and space communications where qualification requirements are stringent.

name: MOS Plastics Inc
old_description: Your solution partner for innovative product development and manufacturer of Medical, Diagnostic, and Pharmaceutical products.  Currier MOS Plastics is ISO 13485 certified and FDA registered regional contract manufacturer offering facilities in Central NY and Southern California.
about:
Currier MOS Plastics operates from San Jose, California, with additional facilities in Central New York and Southern California. The company traces its roots to 1982, when Currier Plastics began pursuing a vision of raising service and quality standards in the molding industry. Ownership structure and founder names are not disclosed in public sources.

The company provides turnkey injection molding and blow molding services for Class II and Class III medical devices, running horizontal and vertical injection molding machines inside ISO Class 7 and ISO Class 8 cleanrooms. Capabilities extend to insert molding, two-shot molding, over-molding, and a range of secondary operations including ultrasonic welding, pad and plate printing, cleanroom assembly, kitting, and component preparation. The firm emphasizes end-to-end support from design-for-manufacturing engineering through full-dimensional layout inspection and statistical process control.

Currier MOS Plastics serves medical device, pharmaceutical, drug delivery, diagnostics, life science, and consumer health markets, along with personal care, packaging, consumer products, telecommunications, electronics, and food and beverage sectors. Named customers include Abbott, Agilent, Allergan, and Cepheid, for whom the company produces fluidic components, diagnostic test kits, surgical instruments, implants, syringes, catheters, and electronic device housings.

The company cites its V² philosophy — value multiplied by velocity — as a guiding principle, supported by a continuous improvement program organized into six pillar teams. A sustainability initiative called the 6 Green Program Directions governs material sourcing and waste reduction across its environmentally focused injection and blow molding operations.

old_description: Located in Michigan and Tennessee, MP Components has grown since 1973 from a model and pattern shop into a solid business that is capable of producing Fixtures and Gauges, Models and Patterns, Molds, Match Metal Dies and Special Machines, along with providing Computer Aided Design (CAD) services. about:
MP Components Inc. traces its roots to the fall of 1973, when Otto Schlatter and Larry Wiersma founded Model Pattern Company Inc. in Byron Center, Michigan. The shop began as a model and pattern operation, handcrafting prototypes for local manufacturers. In January 1996, the company was renamed MP Components to reflect its expanding capabilities. Today, the business remains family-owned, with the founders' sons, Joe and John Schlatter, the second generation from facilities in Byron Center, Michigan, and Cookeville, Tennessee.

The company designs and builds a range of tooling, including checking fixtures (from simple to complex automated units), models and foundry patterns, aluminum vacuum molds, blow molds, foam and compression molds, match-metal trim dies, and special machinery. It also provides computer-aided design (CAD) services, CMM inspection, and CNC machining. Operations span a 28,000-square-foot plant in Michigan and a 10,000-square-foot facility in Tennessee, equipped with current-generation machining and measurement technology.

MP Components serves manufacturers in the automotive, furniture, appliance, aerospace, and medical industries. Its customer base extends across the continental United States, Canada, and Mexico, with the two Midwestern locations positioned for broad geographic coverage.

The founders' original mission — to deliver handcrafted quality models and prototypes — continues to shape the company's approach. MP Components emphasizes a one-stop-shop model for tooling needs, backed by ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 17025 certifications, and highlights rapid turnaround times as a key differentiator.

old_description: Masimo Semiconductor has been developing and manufacturing III-V opto-electronic devices since 1982. about:
Masimo Semiconductor was founded in 1982 in Hudson, New Hampshire, and has since focused on the development and manufacture of III‑V opto‑electronic devices. The privately held company operates from a facility in Hudson.

The company specializes in wafer epitaxy, foundry services, and device fabrication. Its core processes include GaAs and InP MOCVD epitaxy, custom III‑V epitaxial growth, device fabrication, optical coating evaporation, and device testing. Masimo Semiconductor offers prototype through high‑volume production runs, supported by an on‑site Agnitron A300 MOCVD reactor installed in 2023 and advanced metrology equipment for epitaxial film and device characterization.

Masimo Semiconductor serves the healthcare, industrial, energy, datacom/telecom, security, and consumer products markets. Its components are used in high‑brightness LEDs for medical and commercial applications, as well as in optoelectronics, biomedical devices, and telecommunications systems.

The company positions itself as a cost‑effective product development and manufacturing partner that does not compete with its customers. It emphasizes close collaboration, protection of customer intellectual property, fast turnaround from prototype to volume, and a staff of epitaxy professionals with over 35 years of industry experience. Quality management conforms to ISO 9001:2015.

old_description: Matrix Plastic Products is a premier custom manufacturer specializing in injection molding, moldmaking & assembly with surgical precision.  We partner with medical device manufacturers to engineer, tool up, and produce ultra-precise molded components and sub-assemblies for their most critical applications.
about:
Matrix Plastic Products operates from Wood Dale, Illinois, just outside Chicago. The company traces its roots to 1978 when it began as Matrix Tooling with seven employees and a family tradition of moldmaking craftsmanship. By 1994 the business had expanded into injection molding, and by 2000 it was running volume production in a facility that had doubled in size.

Today Matrix provides injection molding, moldmaking, and assembly with a focus on surgical precision. Its capabilities include scientific and decoupled molding processes, multi-shot molding, and micro molding for miniature components. The shop runs three shifts on presses ranging from 20 to 300 tons, employs 140 people, and is expanding from its current Wood Dale location to an 88,000-square-foot facility in nearby Bloomingdale. An ISO Class 8 cleanroom supports medical-grade molding and assembly.

The company serves global leaders in the medical device, electronics, personal care, and safety industries. Typical projects include minimally invasive surgical instruments, micro medical devices, and high-performance electronic components. Customers rely on Matrix for full traceability and device-history records that meet regulatory requirements.

Matrix differentiates itself through nearly five decades of in-house design-for-manufacturability and moldmaking expertise, a quality system certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016, and a culture that blends traditional craftsmanship with continuous investment in automation and inspection technology. The firm emphasizes reliability, responsiveness, and direct communication between project teams and customers.

about:
Mega Electronics Inc. operates from New Brunswick, New Jersey. Founded in 1984, the company began with the goal of supplying a single source for components that deliver power from the wall into electronic products for any global location. No founders are named in public records, and ownership structure has not been disclosed.

The company designs, manufactures, and distributes power cords, power supplies, and DC/DC converters. Its power supply line spans wall-mount, desktop, DIN-rail, and open-frame formats from 5 W to 960 W, carrying UL, CSA, CE, CCC, CB, and other global safety marks. DC/DC converters range from 0.25 W to 200 W in through-hole, surface-mount, and chassis-mount packages. Mega also produces IEC Lock locking connectors, EN60309 industrial plugs, anti-microbial cables, twist-lock extension cords up to 30 A, and card-edge connectors that mate directly to printed circuit boards. An ISO 9001-certified production facility supports these lines, and a U.S. warehouse enables stock shipment worldwide. The firm offers vendor-managed inventory (VMI), just-in-time (JIT), and kanban programs for blanket and stock-and-release orders.

Mega serves commercial and industrial markets including medical equipment, data centers, computer peripherals, food-service machinery, industrial equipment, networking hardware, and vending machines. Its power cords hold approvals for North America, Europe, Asia, Australia, South America, and the Middle East, allowing customers to ship products globally without separate cord qualifications.

The company cites three pillars—high-quality products, excellent customer service, and superior product knowledge—as its foundation. It emphasizes single-stop shopping for power components, worldwide approval expertise, dedicated engineering support from concept through product life cycle, and a stock-based fulfillment model backed by VMI, JIT, and kanban services.

name: Melink Solar
old_description: Since 1987, Melink Solar has been helping organizations of all sizes create a sustainable future. We became a leader in renewable energy when we built one of the nation’s first LEED Platinum-certified buildings, demonstrating the business case for clean energy. In 2008, we launched our solar division and have since installed over 275 MW across the U.S. Our experience spans projects of all scales, from small commercial installations to large utility-scale arrays, always delivering tailored solutions to meet each customer’s unique needs. Known for our expertise and commitment to quality, we’re proud that so many of our clients return to work with us on future projects. Whether it’s a first-time installation or part of a long-term energy strategy, we’re here to guide you toward a more sustainable future.
about:
Melink Solar, headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, traces its roots to 1987 when engineer and entrepreneur Steve Melink founded Melink Corporation as an HVAC testing and balancing firm. Melink's invention of the Intelli-Hood variable-speed control system for commercial kitchen ventilation became an industry standard, establishing the company's focus on energy efficiency.

In 2008, the company launched its solar division, Melink Solar, as a full-service commercial EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) provider delivering turnkey projects that encompass system design and engineering, material procurement, construction, and operations and maintenance. The firm has installed more than 275 megawatts and 650,000 panels across the United States, ranging from small commercial rooftops to a 15‑megawatt utility-scale array in Piqua, Ohio, and it owns and operates 10 megawatts of solar capacity.

Melink Solar serves independent power producers, utilities, commercial and industrial facilities, schools and universities, religious organizations, municipalities, government agencies, and non‑profits. Notable clients include the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, and the parent corporation has worked with brands such as Apple, Google, Walmart, and Disney.

The company's differentiation stems from its demonstrated commitment to sustainability: its Cincinnati headquarters achieved LEED Platinum and Net Zero Energy status in 2010, among the first 25 buildings worldwide to do so, and Melink Solar tests solar technologies on its own campus before deploying them for customers.

The family ownership structure enables direct access to project managers and quick decision-making, while documented quality practices, traceability, and supply chain support (turnkey, consignment, or hybrid) help reduce risk on complex assemblies.

about:
Midcon Cables Company was founded in 1972 in North Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. The business is employee-owned and operates facilities in both Missouri and South Carolina.

The company manufactures custom and build-to-print cable assemblies, harnesses, and molded interconnects for demanding applications. Its capabilities include cold molding and over-molding per MIL-M-24041, RF coaxial connector and cable assembly termination, fiber optic cable assemblies (single- and multi-mode), and proprietary organized-wiring technologies such as EverFlex and MicroFlex. Engineering design support, qualification testing, and full documentation are provided alongside prototyping and full-rate production.

Midcon serves the aerospace and defense, industrial, and medical markets. Its products are used on aircraft, ground vehicles, missiles, unmanned systems, rotorcraft, ships, and communications platforms. The company also supports commercial customers with value-added wiring solutions.

Midcon differentiates itself with its EverFlex organized-wiring system, which replaces conventional harnesses and flex circuits with a low-profile, robust alternative that integrates controlled circuit positions and tie-downs. A proprietary quick-set potting compound reduces molding cycle times, and the MicroFlex process uses NC machining to produce ultra-flat ribbon assemblies that can incorporate power, signal, RF, and fiber optic lines. The firm holds AS9100 and NADCAP certifications and is recognized as a preferred supplier for its on-time delivery and quality performance.

about:
Mission Plastics Inc. (MPI) was founded in 1982 in Ontario, California, as a custom injection-molding operation. The company is now headquartered in Nashville, Arkansas, and operates additional facilities in Rancho Cucamonga, California, and Mexicali, Mexico. President Robert Guy leads the organization, which has grown into a full-spectrum manufacturer serving medical, automotive, and commercial sectors.

The company provides precision injection molding, overmolding, insert molding, thin-wall molding, and multi-cavity family molding, supported by in-house tool design, mold making, and automation. Secondary services include plastics and metal CNC machining, assembly, and a full metrology lab with CMM and Keyence laser scanning. The Rancho Cucamonga site houses an on-site tool room and metrology lab, while the Mexicali plant runs 40 molding machines ranging from 55 to 400 tons, with press capacity from 7 to 720 tons and a Class 8 clean room for 7–310-ton presses. Both sites operate 24/7 and handle prototype through high-volume production.

Mission Plastics serves medical device OEMs, automotive suppliers, and commercial product manufacturers. Medical customers have included CareFusion/BD (AirLife respiratory consumables), Safety Syringe (a Beckton Dickinson company), and Parker/Legris. Commercial work spans consumer components, electrical enclosures, and irrigation fittings, with Taral Plastic Container Company cited as a long-term partner.

The company emphasizes scientific molding methodologies, including process capability studies via Minitab, design of experiments, and RJG Master Molder expertise. Its quality system is certified to ISO 13485 for medical devices and ISO 9001, with validation capabilities covering IQ/OQ/PQ and PPAP. A nearshore supply chain model, combining U.S. engineering with Mexican production, is positioned to reduce lead times and logistics risk.

Modern Welding Company of Kentucky, Inc. operates from Elizabethtown, Kentucky, tracing its roots to June 1932 when John G. Barnard — known as “Mr. Pete” — opened a small job shop in Owensboro. The company manufactures underground and aboveground steel storage tanks, ASME-code pressure vessels, and LPG tanks for flammable and combustible liquids and gases. Its Elizabethtown facility specializes in custom plate work, chute fabrication, wear products, and structural steel fabrication. Modern Welding runs ten tank and vessel fabrication subsidiaries nationwide, two dedicated structural steel plants, and four welding supply stores in Kentucky and Indiana, all linked by a shared information network.

Customers span energy, construction, distillery, agriculture, defense, mining, chemical processing, and petroleum storage. Documented projects include a refinery deisohexanizer tower, UL-142 emergency fuel tanks installed within a hospital footprint, high-capacity fuel storage for a global agribusiness, and bulk propane tanks for poultry facility heating.

Modern Welding positions itself as the largest U.S. supplier of UL-listed steel storage tanks. Its quality program encompasses ASME, NBIC, AWS, AISC, UL, STI, and API standards, and the Elizabethtown plant holds AISC Certified Fabricator status. The company emphasizes domestic production, a regional subsidiary model for faster delivery, and a guaranteed 24-hour quote turnaround.

about:
OE Solar is headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The company was founded in 2009 as Osceola Energy, Inc. with the original goal of installing solar across the state. It is a woman‑owned small business that rebranded to OE Solar as its focus expanded to enterprise‑level renewable energy solutions for both private and public sector clients.

The firm operates as a full‑service engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractor for commercial solar photovoltaic systems, battery energy storage systems (BESS), EV charging infrastructure, solar carports, and microgrid installations. It also provides operations and maintenance, community solar development, and pre‑construction planning.

OE Solar serves commercial and industrial businesses, federal, state, and local government agencies, Tribal Nations, military installations, educational institutions, and hospitality venues. Named clients include Santa Ana Casino, Santa Ana Golf Club, Albuquerque Public Schools, and the Picuris Pueblo — for whom the company built New Mexico’s first community solar project.

The company emphasizes its GSA‑approved, woman‑owned small business status, NABCEP certification, and Tesla and ChargePoint certified installers as differentiators. It also highlights deep expertise in government energy policy, established relationships with regulators and policymakers, and a founding philosophy built on honesty, craftsmanship, and ownership.

Obertron Electronic Manufacturing has operated from Manchester, Michigan since its founding in 1986. The company provides PCB assembly services from a single Midwestern facility, emphasizing skilled craftsmanship and responsive service.

The shop specializes in medium-volume, high-mix PCBA assembly, combining automated surface-mount placement (including 01005, QFN, BGA, and fine-pitch components) with through-hole selective and hand soldering. Customers span LED lighting, service industries (commercial, hospitality, healthcare), test and measurement, instrumentation, industrial equipment, medical and health devices, aerospace and automotive (including EV), agriculture and industrial automation, commercial and recreational electronics, and R&D prototypes.

Obertron differentiates itself through lean manufacturing, ongoing staff training, flexible production scheduling, and a standard 5–6 week lead time. A one-year labor warranty and transparent quoting reinforce its focus on dependable partnerships.

old_description: Founded in 1958, Ohio Steel Industries began business with one employee operating principally as a structural steel fabricator, in a 25,000 square feet facility in Columbus, Ohio. Our market and delivery area then was the central Ohio area. Our company today operates in multiple facilities and locations of more than 300,000 square feet providing material, products and services throughout the world.
about:
Ohio Steel Industries was founded in 1958 in Columbus, Ohio, when a single employee began operating a structural steel fabrication shop in a 25,000-square-foot facility serving central Ohio. The company has since expanded to multiple locations totaling more than 300,000 square feet and serves customers worldwide.

The business operates through three divisions. The Manufacturing Division provides contract fabrication of lawn and garden riding mower attachments, utility trailers, loading ramps, and display merchandising, using processes that include stamping, welding, bending, cutting, forming, powder coating, packaging, and shipping. OSI Plastics, an ISO 9001:2015-registered division, produces extruded plastic profiles for utilities, telecommunications firms, and other large enterprises across the United States and Europe. The Structural Steel Division, housed in a 120,000-square-foot plant in Pataskala, fabricates, furnishes, and erects structural steel for buildings and bridges and holds AISC certification for standard, simply supported, and major bridge structures.

Customers range from retail mass merchants and OEM lawn-and-garden manufacturers to distributors, dealers, public utilities, and telecommunications companies. The structural division serves the construction sector, while the plastics division supplies large publicly traded companies. Products are shipped globally, with a particular presence in the U.S. and European markets.

The company states its commitments as providing a safe workplace, exceeding customer expectations in quality and delivery, expanding its market through research and development, developing and retaining its workforce, and creating jobs in its community. Its differentiators include AISC-certified structural fabrication, ISO 9001:2015 registration for plastics, and full-service metal fabrication under one roof.

about:
Orion Plastics Inc. was founded in 2001 in Compton, California, as a custom manufacturer of polyethylene bags, sheeting, and tubing. The company operates from a single location in Compton with several extrusion lines.

The company produces a wide range of polyethylene products including bags (box liners, bin liners, pallet covers, hazardous waste bags, furniture and mattress bags), sheeting (agricultural, mulch film, shrink bundling, anti-static), and tubing (anti-static, shrink, perforated, continuous on roll). Its extrusion lines are capable of producing millions of pounds of product annually, supported by printing capabilities (1C-2S and 2C-1S) and converting equipment for loose bags, roll bags, and gusseted configurations up to 144 inches wide. Gauges run up to 0.010 inch, with standard 3-inch ID cores and roll diameters from 8 to 30 inches.

Orion serves customers in food processing (FDA compliant and SQF certified), agriculture, construction, hazardous waste management, asbestos abatement, furniture and bedding, and textile industries. Specific product examples include FDA-compliant box liners, agricultural mulch film, hazardous waste bags, asbestos removal bags, and furniture and mattress bags.

The company emphasizes flexibility without sacrificing dependability, offering custom sizing, venting options, slip levels, and leak-proof seals. Its FDA compliance and SQF certification support food-contact applications.

old_description: "The team at P&M Apparel are fantastic.  Timely, communicative, and thoughtful about their work.  I worked with a few different people at P&M and all of them listened well to what we needed and were able to translate our needs/vision into something tangible.  The quality of the materials and print were excellent.  The people are even better.  Definitely recommend."
about:
P & M Apparel operates from Polk City, Iowa, where it was founded in 1987 by Phyllis and Melvin — the P and M — after careers in farming and home remodeling. The business began in their basement and moved to Polk City as it grew. Their daughter Kay took over leadership, and in 2023 ownership passed to the third generation: Megan Griffith and Ryan Toney. The company is certified as woman-owned and remains family-run.

The shop provides screen printing, embroidery, direct-to-film digital printing, vinyl, glitter, rhinestone, puff, and sublimation decoration, plus live event printing, online team stores, and promotional product sourcing. With a crew of 16, the facility handles orders ranging from a single piece to runs exceeding 10,000 units. All artwork is created in-house, and every job receives a proof before production.

Customers include schools, sports teams, businesses, nonprofits, dance studios, churches, and community organizations across Iowa and nationally. The company has shipped to 29 countries and produces state tournament apparel with no rush fees, corporate swag, fundraising merchandise, and uniform programs.

The founders’ philosophy centers on “great apparel builds belonging” and a service model that prioritizes fast answers, kept promises, and problem-solving over transactional decoration. Roughly 90 percent of business comes from referrals, a result the owners attribute to acting as a single partner for all decoration methods rather than a vendor list.

name: PREMOLD CORP
old_description: On June 30th, 2022, Ken Schweitz sadly passed away. As a founder and president since 1995, Ken’s tremendous work ethic, high standards, and dedication to the company, employees, and customers have helped Premold Corp become North America’s largest supplier of World-Class Reaction Injection Molding. His values and standards have become engrained in Premold’s culture and will ensure enormous support for continuous success and growth going forward. By leaving behind his legacy of what Premold Corp has become the team thanks Ken Schweitz for all his work and care over the past decades.
about:
Premold Corp was founded in 1995 by Ken Schweitz in Oconomowoc, Wisconsin. The privately owned company operates two facilities in Oconomowoc and a third in Monterrey, Mexico. After Ken Schweitz's passing in 2022, his daughter Ximena Schweitz assumed the presidency, continuing the family's leadership in reaction injection molding (RIM).

The company specializes in reaction injection molding, producing rigid polyurethane parts for low-volume and prototype applications. Its capabilities span in-house tool making with CNC-machined aluminum molds, cast urethane and stereolithography prototyping, short-run production with just-in-time delivery, finish painting using Sherwin Williams Polane coatings, UL-recognized EMI shielding, silk-screen and pad-print graphics, and full assembly including procurement and sub-assembly. The RIM process allows complex geometries, varying wall thicknesses without sink marks, and molded-in features that eliminate secondary machining.

Premold serves a range of industries with a focus on medical and laboratory instrumentation, supplying molded housings, bezels, and skins. Customers include medical device manufacturers requiring custom low-volume polyurethane components.

The company differentiates itself through a single-source model that integrates tooling, molding, finishing, and assembly under one roof, reducing lead times and enabling design-for-manufacture collaboration from prototype through production.

Pacific Auto Company, operating as Pacific Best Inc., was established in 1983 in Paramount, California, within the Los Angeles metropolitan area. The company began as a warehouse distributor of automotive collision body parts and cooling products, serving the Southern California repair market.

Today, Pacific Auto Company maintains six distribution centers across Southern California, supported by over nine warehouses and a dedicated delivery fleet. The company emphasizes competitive pricing on every order and a quality administration system designed to streamline ordering and same-day dispatch.

name: Peace River Packing Company
old_description: A family-owned and operated producer of fresh citrus from our location in historic Fort Meade, Florida. Since 1928, our business has grown by harvesting and packing premium oranges, tangerines, and grapefruit for customers across the globe.
about:
Peace River Packing Company operates from Fort Meade, Florida. Founded in 1928 by a group of local citrus growers who pooled resources to build their own packinghouse, the business has remained family-owned and operated. It later became an agricultural cooperative and a member of Florida’s Natural Growers in 1970.

The company manages and harvests more than 2,000 acres of citrus groves across Polk, Highlands, and Hillsborough counties, and packs oranges, tangerines, and grapefruit. Its facility includes high-speed electronic fruit graders, automated bagging machines, and a large multilevel cooler. With over 130 employees, it is the largest private employer in Fort Meade and ranks among the top 20 fresh citrus packinghouses in Florida by production volume.

Peace River serves the fresh citrus market, supplying fruit to customers globally through the Florida’s Natural Growers cooperative. Its primary industries are citrus production, fresh fruit packing, and agricultural cooperatives.

The founders established the packinghouse to give local growers collective control over packing and marketing, a structure that continues as a cooperative today.

name: Pegasus Foods Inc
old_description: With over 50 years of combined culinary innovation, we specialize in manufacturing high-quality frozen appetizers, including rangoon scoops, empanadas, egg rolls, burritos, poppers, bulk fillings, and desserts. As a trusted contract manufacturer, we partner with national consumer brands, leading supermarket retailers, food service distributors, and QSRs to deliver these exceptional frozen appetizer and meal solutions.
about:
Pegasus Food Group was founded in 1998 in Los Angeles, California as a family business. After two decades of growth, the company relocated its operations to Rockwall, Texas in 2018 to support expanded production capacity. The business began with a focus on culinary creativity and has since evolved into a full-service co-manufacturer of frozen appetizers, snacks, and meal solutions.

Today the company operates a 135,000-square-foot SQF-certified USDA facility in Rockwall equipped with seven production lines. Capabilities include dough extrusion and co-extrusion, automated and hand-rolled forming, inline frying and baking, batter and breading, ammonia-based freezing, and X-ray inspection. An in-house culinary R&D team supports product development from ideation through commercialization, leveraging equipment such as Rheon and Vemag systems. The facility produces a range of frozen items including rangoon scoops, empanadas, egg rolls, burritos, poppers, bulk fillings, and desserts.

Pegasus serves national consumer brands, supermarket retailers, club stores, quick-service and casual-dining restaurant chains, and foodservice distributors. It also manages private-label programs for major grocery and club channels and markets its own brands, By the Bite and The Perfect Bite Co. Client relationships are often confidential; testimonials reference retail, foodservice, and emerging-brand partners who value the company’s responsiveness and consistency at scale.

The company positions itself on a combination of scale and agility: a large certified facility paired with a “nimble” operating model that emphasizes quick response, rapid changeover, and fast time-to-market.

name: Pennsylvania Transformer Technology, LLC.
old_description: Pennsylvania Transformer Technology, founded in 1929, is a U.S.-owned transformer manufacturer under Quanta Services, blending legacy expertise with modern engineering at two domestic facilities. Headquartered in Canonsburg, PA—formerly home to McGraw-Edison and Cooper Power Systems—the company also operates a Raeford, NC plant producing transformers for nearly 30 years. Proven designs, proven processes—experience matters.
about:
Pennsylvania Transformer Technology (PTT) traces its roots to 1929 in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, where the company now occupies a 1-million-square-foot, 18-building campus on 90 acres — a site that previously housed McGraw-Edison and Cooper Power Systems transformer operations. The business is a U.S.-owned subsidiary of Quanta Services, a North American infrastructure firm, and operates a second domestic plant in Raeford, North Carolina, built in 1992 on 10 acres with 56,000 square feet of production space.

PTT designs and manufactures oil-filled power transformers ranging from 500 kVA to 750 MVA with voltage ratings through 765 kV, including generator step-up, autotransformers, pad-mount, unit substation, mobile, and specialty industrial transformers. The Canonsburg facility features North America’s largest GEORG automatic core cutting and stacking line, a 200,000-square-foot tank fabrication bay, 500-ton lifting capacity, and test capability to 765 kV/2400 kV BIL. Beyond new builds, the Power Solutions division provides full lifecycle services: field installation, preventive maintenance, oil processing, repairs, refurbishment, engineering studies (loading, cooling, condition assessment, life extension, stray flux), and authorized replacement parts for load tap changers and circuit breakers from legacy brands such as McGraw-Edison, Cooper Power, and Federal Pacific. The Green Core division handles transformer decommissioning and recycling nationwide.

The company serves electric utilities, data centers, renewable energy developers (solar, wind), battery energy storage systems (BESS), heavy industrial manufacturing, and power generation. Its transformers are deployed in utility substations, hyperscale data centers, and grid-integration projects for renewables and storage.

PTT emphasizes its nearly 100 years of continuous transformer engineering, dual U.S. production sites, ISO 9001:2015 with Design certification, and the backing of Quanta Services as factors that differentiate it from overseas suppliers and enable support for large-scale infrastructure projects.

name: Phase Electronics
old_description: Phase Electronics strives to be a leader in quality. Our policy is continuous improvement through customer satisfaction. 100% of our assemblies are inspected by hand or automated optical inspection (AOI) machines to verify a quality assembly.
about:
Phase Electronics is a privately owned, family-run electronics manufacturer based in Rockville, Maryland. The company was established in 1984 by David Regnier, who remains president and owner, and has operated continuously as a small family business since its inception.

Operating from an owner-occupied 26,000-square-foot facility, Phase Electronics provides a range of electronic manufacturing services including rapid prototyping, medium-volume production, surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, electromechanical box builds, cable assemblies, rework, conformal coating, X-ray inspection, and programming and testing. The plant is fully ESD-safe and equipped with modern machinery, including automated optical inspection systems. The staff consists of long-tenured, IPC-trained employees, many with 15-plus years at the company.

The company serves customers in the commercial, military, medical, and automotive sectors, delivering assemblies built to IPC-A-610 Class 2 standards with Class 3 available on request. All personnel handling assemblies are trained to J-STD-001 with the space addendum.

Phase Electronics emphasizes a direct line to the manufacturing floor for real-time issue resolution, 100 percent inspection via automated optical inspection and hand checks, and compliance with J-STD-001 including the space addendum. The firm is ITAR registered, holds ISO 9001:2015 certification, and is SAM registered, aiming to provide quality manufacturing at reasonable prices within customer time constraints.

name: Polar Wire Products
old_description: We are a renowned manufacturer of premium industrial-grade wire designed to withstand even the harshest environments. Our finely stranded wire configurations are proudly made in the USA and used among a variety of applications from recreational equipment to the development of the latest revolutionary technology.
about:
Polar Wire Products was founded in 1991 in Anchorage, Alaska, as a family-owned business. From its humble beginnings in Alaska, the company expanded to key locations in the lower 48 states while maintaining its headquarters and manufacturing in Anchorage.

The company manufactures premium industrial-grade wire, most notably its flagship Arctic Ultraflex Blue® and Arctic Superflex Blue® lines, which are rated for continuous operation from -55°C to 105°C and use 100% copper conductors with no aluminum. In addition to wire manufacturing, Polar Wire provides custom cable assembly services built to IPC/WHMA-A-620 Class 3 standards, wholesale distribution of solderless terminals, compression and mechanical lugs, heat shrink, and other wiring control products and tools. Its facilities offer engineering services and technical review, precision cutting and stripping, and high-quality crimping, with capacity ranging from rapid prototyping to large-scale production. Thousands of fittings and products are stocked for quick turnaround.

Polar Wire serves a broad customer base that includes the general public, government agencies, OEMs, stocking distributors, and fleet accounts. Its products are used in renewable energy, telecommunications, automotive, fleet, commercial, industrial, and recreational applications. Finished assemblies appear as battery cables, jumper cables, extension cords, shore power and generator leads, and stage and lighting cords.

The company emphasizes its hands-on control of every stage from design to assembly, citing superior quality, exceptional customer service, and competitive pricing as differentiators. Its wire has been proven in extreme environments from Alaska's North Slope to Antarctica, and the team carries over 200 years of combined industry experience. Polar Wire aims for long-term, mutually beneficial partnerships and offers private-label/OEM manufacturing with custom configurations, colors, striping, and print legends.

about:
Precision Cable Assemblies Inc. (PCA) was founded in 1980 in Brookfield, Wisconsin, a suburb of Milwaukee. The company began as a wire harness manufacturer and has since expanded into a global supplier of power distribution solutions.

PCA manufactures wire harnesses ranging from single-circuit assemblies to complex designs with over 300 circuits, battery cables and interconnects, and custom overmolded cable assemblies. Over the following decades the company expanded into full-service custom injection molding and precision machining. In 2020 the operation was acquired by Precision Molding & Machining, which continues to run the facility as a privately held shop serving the western United States.

The shop combines plastic injection molding with a complete machine shop under one roof. Press capacity spans 75 to 350 tons, with additional presses on order. Machining capabilities include four vertical CNC mills equipped with fourth-axis rotary tables, two EDM units, surface grinders, and manual lathes and mills. This equipment mix allows the team to produce molded components, build and maintain tooling, and finish parts to tight specifications in a single facility.

Customers come from military, medical device, material handling, automotive, and specialty electronics sectors. The company emphasizes long-term partnerships that take projects from concept through finished production, supplying both molded and machined components to OEMs and contract manufacturers across the western U.S.

The acquisition was driven by a goal to establish the region's go-to custom molder and machine shop, backed by ISO 9001:2015 certification and an in-house tooling heritage that shortens lead times on new programs.

name: Precision Textiles
old_description: Founded in 1987 as Precision Custom Coatings by Peter Longo, the current chairman of what would become Precision Textiles, the company began as a supplier of interlinings to distributors and fabric wholesalers working within the apparel industry. When the apparel business shifted offshore, Scott Tesser, today’s chief executive officer, joined the company and established a business-model in Asia, allowing the company’s customers easier access to products in high demand.
about:
Precision Textiles is headquartered in Totowa, New Jersey. The company traces its roots to 1987 when Peter Longo founded Precision Custom Coatings as a supplier of interlinings to apparel distributors and fabric wholesalers. Longo remains chairman. Scott Tesser, now chief executive officer and co-owner, joined the business after the apparel trade moved offshore and built an Asia-based supply model for customers. In 2000 Longo and Tesser bought back the company from a private-equity owner and renamed it Precision Textiles to pursue markets beyond apparel.

Today the firm designs, produces and globally distributes fire-retardant nonwovens, laminates, coated fabrics and specialty fibers from a 210,000-square-foot headquarters that houses a state-of-the-art laboratory, factory and warehouse. Four additional U.S. warehouses and three overseas joint-venture warehouses extend its reach. An in-house R&D team operates around the clock to develop and lab-test solutions for bedding, automotive and healthcare applications.

Customers include mattress and sleep-product manufacturers, automotive OEMs and tier suppliers, and healthcare product makers. In the automotive sector the company has supplied materials for speaker components, upholstery liners, dashboard and door-panel insulation, and headliners. For bedding it provides a range of glass-free flame-barrier products such as ECOFLEX, IQFit Natural and the GOTS-certified PureLoft wool barrier.

The shift into bedding was driven by the 2004 federal open-flame mattress standard. Precision Textiles emphasizes environmentally conscious methods: solar panels at its factory, GOTS-certified organic wool, and a portfolio of recyclable, non-allergenic fibers. Its Precision Cares program donates bedding and furniture to non-profits serving children, veterans and domestic-abuse survivors.

The company emphasizes a history of customer-awarded recognition for vendor excellence, quality assurance, safety, cost control, and innovation. name: Production Science Inc
old_description: Production Sciences, Inc. has been in operation since June 1989. The business was founded in and is still located in Chestertown, Maryland. All manufacturing is still performed at this location in the USA!
about:
Production Sciences, Inc. has operated from Chestertown, Maryland since its founding in June 1989. The company remains at its original location on Dixon Drive, conducting all manufacturing domestically.

The firm produces soft plastic components through dip molding, dip coating, and plastisol casting. Dip molding creates connectors, caps, and sleeves by dipping heated metal forms into liquid plastisol, curing, and stripping the finished part. Dip coating applies protective or aesthetic plastisol layers onto customer-supplied metal parts such as brackets, hooks, and spring latches. Plastisol casting pours liquid material into metal molds to form solid objects, which can be die-cut and given adhesive backings for marker applications. An onsite machine shop builds and iterates tooling, enabling concept-to-sample turnaround in as little as one week. Modeling services use SolidWorks to generate 2D drawings and 3D models from customer concepts or existing files. The company states it handles components of all quantities and physical sizes, scaling from prototype to full production runs.

Medical device manufacturers worldwide are a primary customer base, with the company highlighting clean, non-sterile production for sensitive applications and experience with radiopaque compounds. Industrial clients also use the service for protective coatings and colored components. Specific examples cited include elongated caps for medical devices, coated spring latches, and protective brackets.

Production Sciences emphasizes its domestic footprint, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and material versatility — offering phthalate-free, medical-grade transparent, and opaque colored plastisols with additives such as scents and radiopaque fillers. The onsite tooling capability is presented as a key enabler for rapid prototyping and cost-effective scaling.

old_description: At Proterial Cable America, we’ve been at the forefront of progress since 1986, manufacturing innovative materials and components for advanced communication networks, life-saving medical equipment, forward-thinking automotive technologies, and defense contracting solutions.
about:
Proterial Cable America, Inc. traces its roots to 1986 when Hitachi Cable America established a manufacturing facility in Manchester, New Hampshire. The company, now a subsidiary of Proterial Ltd. (formerly Hitachi Metals), rebranded to its current name as part of a global corporate identity shift. From its New Hampshire headquarters, the business has expanded to eight manufacturing sites worldwide, including locations in Indiana, Mexico, Rhode Island, and Connecticut.

The company operates through three divisions. The Performance Cable Systems & Materials Division produces copper and fiber optic communication cables and assemblies supporting Ethernet, video, Power over Ethernet, HDMI, and InfiniBand applications. The Automotive Products Division supplies original equipment manufacturers and Tier 1 suppliers with power cable harnesses for electric and hybrid vehicles, brake hoses, electronic parking brake harnesses, wheel speed sensors, and torque sensors. The High Performance Medical Solutions Division, certified to ISO 13485:2016, provides complex catheter tubing, braided and high-pressure braided tubing, secondary operations, medical machining, fabrication, 3D additive manufacturing, cable assemblies, and full device assembly for products such as PICC catheters, introducer sheaths, fluid transport tubing, ultrasound devices, endoscopic camera catheters, and advanced diagnostic or surgical catheters. The combined facilities offer both high-volume production and rapid prototyping capabilities.

Proterial Cable America serves four primary sectors: data communications OEMs requiring high-performance connectivity; medical device OEMs needing precision extrusion and assembly; automotive OEMs and major Tier 1s sourcing brake and sensor systems; and defense contractors requiring ITAR-compliant manufacturing. Customers include manufacturers of networking equipment, minimally invasive surgical devices, electric vehicle platforms, and military communication systems.

The company emphasizes a "Professional, Proactive, Progressive" approach, highlighting long-term customer relationships, rigorous quality control under ISO 9001:2015, and a safety-first culture across all divisions. Its engineering team of 43 specialists works to integrate design, compliance, and manufacturing to accelerate customer innovation.

old_description: Proxy Manufacturing, Inc. is an Electronic Contract Manufacturer servicing Massachusetts, New England, and the United States since 1988. Proxy has a 30-year track record of delivering high quality, being competitive, and being easy to do business with. about:
Proxy Manufacturing, Inc. has operated as an electronic contract manufacturer from Methuen, Massachusetts since 1988. The company serves customers across New England and the United States. President Kathleen Dugas leads the business, which holds HUBZone and small-business certifications.

The 30,000-square-foot facility houses three surface-mount lines, a dedicated prototype lab, and separate through-hole and box-build areas. Processes cover prototype and new-product introduction, printed-circuit assembly, system integration, and rework or engineering-change-order implementation. The lines handle leaded and RoHS soldering, placing components as small as 01005, with BGA placement, X-ray inspection, BGA re-balling, mixed-technology assembly, cable assembly, and automated optical inspection. The company supports both quick-turn and volume production runs.

Proxy serves commercial, industrial, defense, and medical markets. Long-term clients include True North Technologies, which has used Proxy as its sole contract manufacturer since 2003 for sensor devices, and Fraunhofer CMI, which relies on the shop for specialized prototype surface-mount devices. The company also works with original equipment manufacturers seeking turnkey or consignment arrangements.

Proxy emphasizes a stable workforce—management, project managers, and team leaders average more than 17 years of tenure—and an IPC-certified in-house trainer. The quality policy targets manufacturing excellence across quick-turn critical orders and turnkey solutions, with certifications including AS9100D, ISO 9001:2015, and ITAR registration.

name: Puritan Medical Products
old_description: Puritan Medical Products is an American family-owned company. We're known worldwide as the most trusted manufacturer of swabs and single-use specimen collection devices for healthcare, diagnostics, forensics, controlled environments and environmental sciences.
about:
Puritan Medical Products, founded in 1919 as Hardwood Products Company, operates from Guilford, Maine. The family-owned business rebranded to Puritan Medical Products Company I, LP in January 2023. It began producing single-use items from Northern white birch and evolved into a specialized manufacturer of swabs and specimen collection devices.

The company runs three manufacturing facilities in Maine — Guilford and two in Pittsfield — where it produces swabs, applicators, and single-use medical devices. Capabilities include flocked swab production, custom fill of transport media, an on-site microbiology lab staffed with microbiologists, a state-of-the-art print shop for labeling and packaging, and full R&D prototyping. The Guilford plant uses 100% renewable energy from wood process waste; overall facilities achieve 35% renewable energy. Puritan is an FDA-registered medical device manufacturer since 1978 and holds ISO and CE Mark certifications.

Products serve diagnostics, forensics and genetics, environmental testing, microbiology media, medical, and controlled environments. Customers include distributors, kit manufacturers, OEM partners, and direct buyers through a new D2C channel. Custom projects typically start at 100,000 units, with NDA-protected development, prototype sampling, and custom bar coding.

Puritan emphasizes USA-made manufacturing, consistent quality, and environmental stewardship — recycling 100% of paper, cardboard, and metal waste. Its differentiation rests on integrated in-house capabilities from formulation to packaging, enabling rapid customization for emerging disease detection and bioterrorism testing.

about:
QXMedical, LLC was founded in 2007 in Montreal, Canada, on the principle of delivering uncompromised value and quality in underserved, high-growth segments of the medical device market. The company established its Technology and Manufacturing Center in Saint Paul, Minnesota, in 2010, positioning itself in the North American medical device hub. Today, its headquarters are in Roseville, Minnesota. Leadership includes CEO Frank Panarello, who founded electronics manufacturing services provider Trilogix EMS in 1990, and President & Chief Technical Officer Fernando Di Caprio, a serial med-tech founder with over 20 medical device patents.

The company designs and manufactures first-in-class medical devices for minimally invasive coronary, peripheral, and endovascular interventions, as well as emergency and trauma care. Its product portfolio includes balloon catheters, delivery catheters, occlusion balloon catheters, stent graft balloon catheters, embolization particles (such as the i-FLEX line), and guide extensions. Manufacturing occurs at its state-of-the-art facility in Saint Paul, though specific facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

QXMedical serves medical device companies of all sizes, including some of the largest U.S. medical device manufacturers, as well as healthcare professionals and strategic partners. Its devices are used in procedures such as vascular disease treatment, embolization therapy, coronary and peripheral artery disease, and hemorrhage control (including REBOA for trauma care).

The company was started to address unmet needs in complex, minimally invasive procedures, leveraging proprietary technology platforms to deliver unique, high-performance devices with unmatched quality. It emphasizes simplifying complex procedures through innovative, simple solutions.

old_description: Quality Snack Foods, Inc. was started in 1986 in the stockyards area of Chicago, Illinois. The company was founded to manufacture pork rinds and pork crackling pellets. about:
Quality Snack Foods Inc. began in 1986 in Chicago's historic stockyards district, founded to produce pork rinds and crackling pellets. The operation relocated in 1990 to the city's Back of the Yards neighborhood, expanding its "pop and pack" capabilities. In 2008 the company moved into a 105,000-square-foot, USDA-inspected facility in Alsip, Illinois, where it remains headquartered.

The Alsip plant houses state-of-the-art cookers, fryers, and packaging lines that turn out pork rinds, cracklings, chicken-skin snacks, chicharrones, fried harina (wheat-flour snacks), and pre-cooked bacon for food-service channels. The vertically integrated operation controls every step from raw-material sourcing through seasoning, frying, and final packaging, allowing flexible run sizes and custom seasoning blends.

Primary customers are private-label brands, food-service distributors, and wholesale buyers across the United States. The company's bacon products are tailored for pizza toppings, salads, appetizers, and even novelty items such as bacon-topped donuts, while its pork-rind and harina lines serve retail snack aisles and keto-focused markets.

Quality Snack Foods emphasizes its SQF certification, on-site USDA inspection, and the "Quality" name as a commitment to consistent product safety and cleanliness. The founders' collective 90-plus years in meat and snack processing underpin the company's focus on vertical integration as a means to maintain strict quality control from source to shelf.

name: Quantum Plastics
old_description: Founded in 2014, Quantum Plastics, LLC was created as a holding company by Quantum Ventures of Michigan. With 5 manufacturing locations, Quantum Plastics produces parts for almost every industry across North America.
about:
Quantum Plastics, LLC is headquartered in Fort Smith, Arkansas. The company was founded in 2014 as a holding company by Quantum Ventures of Michigan. It operates five manufacturing locations across North America, including divisions in Elgin, Gladewater, Juarez, Raleigh, and Victor.

The company specializes in custom injection molding, blow molding, and assembly. Its processes include gas assist molding, insert molding, two-shot molding, and custom injection molding on presses ranging from 30 to 3,000 tons. Quantum Plastics runs 230 molding presses across its facilities and offers in-house engineering and tooling, integrated product development, assembly and decorating options, and robotic automation. It processes hundreds of resin grades, colorants, and additives per customer specifications.

Quantum Plastics serves the automotive, appliance, medical, food-contact, consumer, and industrial markets. Automotive programs require tight tolerances and structural performance, while blow-molded products such as the Kosmo Cooler and Safe Keeper demonstrate its consumer and industrial reach. The company's quality systems align with program-specific requirements across these sectors.

Quantum Plastics emphasizes quality engineered into every stage, from tooling design and material handling to process setup and final release. Its approach centers on designing for manufacturability, with tooling and engineering teams evaluating mold design, part geometry, and resin behavior early in development. Certifications including ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015, and NSF support controlled processes, traceability, and nonconformance management.

Rapport emphasizes cost savings through efficient processes and long-term partnerships. Its stated mission is to act as a strategic manufacturing partner, allowing customers to focus on core competencies while Rapport handles component, battery, and cable assembly needs. The company highlights its use of Kanban and JIT to improve throughput and delivery timelines, as well as its ISO 9001:2015 certification and adherence to UL/CSA and RoHS standards as differentiators.

name: Ready Foods
old_description: With this vision, Ready Foods was founded to supply foodservice operators with quality recipes to be scaled with consistency. Soon after, the Marco's product line was created to provide restaurants with an economical way to serve authentic Mexican cuisine on their menu, based on Luis Abarca’s heritage. Although we have grown from our original kitchen on Colfax Avenue, the Abarca's philosophy continues to provide a vision for Ready Foods over fifty years later. Through years of expansion to our current multi-facility production space, we stand by the integrity of our food, our collective knowledge and the expertise of our workforce.
about:
Ready Foods was founded in 1972 by immigrant Luis Abarca in Denver, Colorado. The family-owned company began as a small kitchen on Colfax Avenue, aiming to provide foodservice operators with consistent, scalable recipes. Soon after, the Marco's product line was launched to offer authentic Mexican cuisine based on Abarca's heritage. Today, the Abarca family still leads the business, which has expanded into a multi-facility operation.

The company operates as a custom food purveyor and private-label co-packer, producing ready-to-use sauces, soups, salsas, beans, tamales, and tortillas. An in-house R&D team develops custom formulations, and products are packaged in five-pound bags with a six-month frozen shelf life. The workforce numbers around 100 employees.

Ready Foods serves independent and chain restaurants, national and regional accounts, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, caterers, hotels, and event venues. Its products reach customers through major broadline distributors. The company also supports foodservice operators facing labor shortages by providing consistent, ready-to-heat items that reduce prep time.

The founder's original vision was to solve labor-driven inconsistency in commercial kitchens as diverse cuisines became mainstream. Ready Foods emphasizes a glass-free facility, paperless quality assurance, and BRC-certified food safety. Its mission stresses safe, high-quality food, employee-centered culture, and community impact, while its vision focuses on empowering customers and teams through delicious recipes.

name: Reliance Packaging
old_description: The Sigma Plastics Group was founded in 1978 by Alfred Teo and is the largest privately owned film extrusion group in North America. Based in Pompano Beach, Florida, the company has over 40 manufacturing facilities producing an annual throughput of over 2 billion pounds of resin. Sigma manufactures a variety of flexible packaging products servicing the industrial, agricultural, food, medical, retail, and converter film markets.
about:
Reliance Packaging operates a 160,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Aberdeen, North Carolina, as a member of the Sigma Plastics Group. The Sigma Plastics Group was founded in 1978 by Alfred Teo and has grown into the largest privately owned film extrusion group in North America, with over 40 facilities and an annual throughput exceeding 2 billion pounds of resin. Reliance Packaging functions as a product specialist within this network, focusing on heavy-duty bags and printed films for specific market segments.

The company extrudes, prints, and converts heavy-duty bags and printed roll-stock using five blown extrusion lines, wide-web flexographic presses, and bag-converting equipment. Its extrusion capacity reaches 20 million pounds annually with a maximum web width of 90 inches and roll outer diameters up to 30 inches. Printing is handled by a 52-inch Schiavi six-color press, a 50-inch PCMC INFINITI eight-color press, and a 50-inch inline flexographic press. Converting includes three side-weld bag machines. A turnkey in-house graphic design department supports custom artwork and plate preparation.

Reliance Packaging serves the lawn and garden, ice-bag, industrial, food, and agricultural markets. Its product line includes mulch and pine bark bags, soil and compost bags, decorative rock bags, play sand and paver base bags, surface-printed and reverse-printed laminated roll stock, food-grade bags and film, freezer-capable ice bags, bailer bags, bags on wickets, industrial bags and films, furniture bags, box and drum liners, and printed industrial shrink film.

The company emphasizes quick turn-around times and quality products, highlighting non-slip ultra-strong film with UV inhibitors and fade-resistant inks designed to perform in tough outdoor conditions. As part of a certified Minority Business Enterprise (NMSDC), Reliance Packaging operates within Sigma Plastics Group's philosophy of domestic manufacturing, sustainability through the How2Recycle program, and independent facility specialization backed by shared capacity.

name: Richmond Auto Parts Technology, Inc
old_description: As a Tier I and II supplier for the automotive industry, Richmond Auto Parts Technology, Inc. about:
Richmond Auto Parts Technology, Inc. (RAPT) operates in Richmond, Kentucky, roughly 36 miles south of Lexington and 10 miles north of Berea. The company was established in 1998 with a $23 million capital investment from its Japanese parent, Aikitec Co., Ltd., and began mass production of automatic transmission gears in July 1999 with an initial team of 20 associates.

RAPT functions as a Tier I and Tier II supplier to the automotive industry, specializing in automatic transmission gears and component parts. The 58-acre campus encompasses a 213,500-square-foot facility staffed by approximately 170 associates. Production capabilities include forging, machining, and assembly for transmissions ranging from 5-speed to 10-speed units, as well as hybrid-electric vehicle (HEV) transmission components. The company has launched programs for 8-speed and 10-speed automatic transmissions and HEV parts.

Primary customers are major Japanese automakers. RAPT has supplied transmission components to Honda since 2000, including 5-speed, 10-speed, and HEV parts, and to Toyota for 8-speed and 10-speed automatic transmissions. The company has received multiple supplier performance awards from both OEMs, including Honda Excellence in Quality and Delivery awards and a Toyota Excellent Quality Performance Award in 2023.

RAPT attributes its differentiation to an associate-centric philosophy summarized in its slogan: “A company that grows strong and survives with associate ideas and knowledge.” The organization emphasizes safety, quality, and production discipline, and maintains ISO 9001:2015 registration. Environmental compliance and community stewardship are also stated priorities.
